detail.abstract: The public web is not a legal free-for-all, and the developing line in automation-risk litigation is more exacting than either slogan. In the summer of 2026, two federal decisions involving the same defendant class pointed in different procedural directions — and together exposed the element the disputes actually turn on: not whether a system accessed public data, but what it did when a technical access control appeared. Four behaviors repeatedly matter because they can be offered as evidence of an attempt to pass an automated system through a control without being recognized for what it is: proxy rotation, IP shifting, false user-agent presentation, and simulated human behavior. These are not automatically unlawful in every setting; paired with an actual access-control process, they can become the factual center of an anti-circumvention claim. The operational consequence is the article's subject: a written policy is not proof of behavior. The operator who can show a fixed method, an ordinary-access path, a tested refusal path, and a record a stranger can verify holds a different answer than the operator who can offer only a policy. Scope: this article explains the allegations and rulings in the authorities cited; it does not conclude that any named company acted unlawfully, and it does not offer legal advice.

title: Generative AI in Personalized Marketing: Effects on Consumer Engagement and Purchase Intention
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Dev Bhoomi Uttarakhand University

detail.title: Generative AI in Personalized Marketing: Effects on Consumer Engagement and Purchase Intention
detail.abstract: The swift spread of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools including large language models and content generators is changing personalized marketing from segment level approaches to direct and individually adaptive brand communication. While there is already a considerable amount of research about GenAI technological capabilities, the systematic knowledge of how personalization based on GenAI influences two core marketing outcomes consumer engagement and purchase intentions remains dispersed through various scholarly disciplines and theoretical traditions. The current paper examines and summarizes recent findings in the field of generative AI use in personalized marketing and applies key theories related to technology acceptance, persuasion, customer engagement, and privacy calculus in order to provide a coherent understanding of the processes by which personalization based on generative AI influences engagement and purchase outcomes. From the review it follows that perceived relevance, trust, anthropomorphism, and transparency are basic moderators enabling successful personalization to lead to positive consumer reactions and prevent them from experiencing privacy related resistance and uncanny valley feelings. The article ends with the overview of the theoretical framework and research agenda for further empirical studies in the area of generative AI use in marketing.

title: Security, Control, and the Illusion of Safety: Psychological Mechanisms Underlying Trust in Password-Protected Digital Wallets after Exposure to Street Crime
affiliations: Shandong University

detail.title: Security, Control, and the Illusion of Safety: Psychological Mechanisms Underlying Trust in Password-Protected Digital Wallets after Exposure to Street Crime
detail.abstract: Background: Street crime is an integral part of life in Pakistan's major cities, and today many payments are made via digital wallets such as password-protected JazzCash, Easypaisa, SadaPay, and NayaPay. This study examines how street crime affects individuals' psychological relationship with the security of their digital wallets and how an illusion of control over digital security might help explain why these tools can be trusted, or even trusted more, after a fear-inducing street crime.Methods: The study used a quantitative, correlational survey distributed to 386 adult users of digital wallets, selected through purposive and stratified sampling in three cities of Karachi, Lahore, and Peshawar, where street crimes have been well documented and are prevalent. Respondents reported their exposure to street-crime activities (direct victimization, witnessing, or none). They completed validated Likert-type scales measuring perceived vulnerability, illusion of control, perceived security, trust in digital wallets, financial-technology anxiety, and continued use intention. We conducted common method bias and normality tests. We tested the hypothesized model using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS, along with t-tests, ANOVA, correlation analysis, and hierarchical regression.Results: Street crime exposure was significantly positively correlated with perceived vulnerability (β = 0.41, p < .001), which in turn was significantly positively correlated with the illusion of control over digital wallet security (β = 0.37, p < .001). Illusion of control was positively correlated with trust in digital wallets (β = 0.33, p < .001), and a serial mediation analysis showed that perceived vulnerability and illusion of control together significantly mediated the effect of crime exposure on trust (indirect effect = 0.051, 95% CI [0.028, 0.079]). However, digital literacy moderated the illusion of control–trust path, with the correlation highest among users with low digital literacy and lowest among digitally literate users. Trust, in turn, better predicted continued use intention than basic perceived security (ΔR² = .07, p < .001).Originality: This is one of the first studies to model the illusion of control as an illusion of safety, rather than as avoidance of financial tools, in the face of fear brought about by street crime. It adds to the studies on fear of crime and on financial-technology-trust by demonstrating how the psychological impact of physical, offline victimization can lead to judgments of other, unrelated, digital risks.Conclusion: Exposure to street crime does not universally erode confidence in digital wallets. For many users, it fosters a naïve sense of control that sustains and can even boost trust in and continued use of digital wallets, especially among less digitally literate people. This finding has implications for consumer protection, financial technology design, and digital-literacy policies in high-crime, rapidly digitizing economies, including Pakistan.

title: When Fit Becomes Too Much: Brand–Content Alignment, Sponsor Salience, and Engagement with Creator Content
affiliations: University of Quebec at Montreal (UQAM), Pontifical Catholic University of Parana and Pontifical Catholic University of Parana

detail.title: When Fit Becomes Too Much: Brand–Content Alignment, Sponsor Salience, and Engagement with Creator Content
detail.abstract: Content creators increasingly integrate sponsored messages into digital content, yet sponsorship introduces a fundamental tension into creator–audience relationships. Existing research also provides mixed evidence regarding how alignment between a sponsoring brand and the surrounding content affects audience engagement. Although congruent sponsorship can increase relevance and endorsement credibility, excessive alignment may also generate perceptions of predominantly commercial motivations and strategic manipulation. To address this issue, this study examines the effects of brand–content fit and sponsor salience on engagement with sponsored creator content using a mixed-methods design. Study 1 conducted a thematic analysis of self-administered online interviews with 51 social media users. The findings show that weak fit is perceived as irrelevant, forced, or opportunistic, whereas excessive fit can make content appear commercially manufactured, scripted, and less authentic. Moderate-to-strong fit is evaluated more favorably when it preserves creator autonomy, credibility, and contextual relevance. Study 2 tested these relationships using 1,296 sponsored YouTube videos and a computational pipeline combining natural language processing, large language models, and semantic embeddings to operationalize brand–content fit. Regression results reveal an inverted U-shaped relationship between brand–content fit and both likes and comments per subscriber. Sponsor salience negatively predicts likes and moderates the curvilinear effect of fit, particularly for this engagement measure. Together, the findings challenge the assumption that greater sponsor–content congruence consistently improves engagement. Practically, creators and sponsors should prioritize relevant but nonintrusive integration while preserving creator autonomy and limiting excessive sponsor visibility.

detail.abstract: Occupational exposure to artificial intelligence is measured with a single number and read as answering two questions at once: how much of a job the technology reaches, and whether it displaces the worker or assists them. Using observed usage from the Anthropic Economic Index, I separate the two. Scope is how much of an occupation's task content observed use reaches; mode is the share of that use taking the automation form instead of the collaborative one. Across nine wave and platform measurements covering 393 to 474 six-digit occupations, employment-weighted correlations between scope and mode lie between 0.03 and 0.21 in absolute value, and seven of the nine bootstrap intervals contain zero. Four widely used exposure indices correlate 0.60 to 0.66 with scope but only 0.09 to 0.38 with mode: the literature has been measuring reach and interpreting it as direction. Mode is also strongly context-dependent, far more automation-heavy in API traffic than in chat. What I measure is the mode of observed use, not a labour-market outcome; the contribution is the measurement precondition for the substitution question.

title: Toward a Conceptual Framework for Digital Distributive Justice in AI-Enabled Work Environments: Explaining Job Satisfaction in Human Resource Management
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Toward a Conceptual Framework for Digital Distributive Justice in AI-Enabled Work Environments: Explaining Job Satisfaction in Human Resource Management
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a transformative force in human resource management (HRM), reshaping employee-related decision-making and raising important concerns about employees' perceptions of fairness. Although AI enhances organizational efficiency, existing organizational justice theories provide limited insight into fairness perceptions in AI-enabled work environments. This study develops a conceptual framework for Digital Distributive Justice as a contemporary extension of traditional distributive justice. The proposed framework explains how technological characteristics, including algorithmic transparency, data quality, and decision explainability, influence employees' fairness perceptions and job satisfaction. Drawing on Organizational Justice Theory, Equity Theory, and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the study positions digital distributive justice as a mediating construct linking AI adoption in HRM to job satisfaction. The study argues that the effectiveness of AI-enabled HRM depends not only on technological capabilities but also on employees' perceptions of fairness and trust in AI-supported decisions. The proposed framework contributes to the organizational justice and digital HRM literature while providing a theoretical foundation for future empirical research.

title: JailAR: Evaluating the Jailbreak Vulnerability of Visual Autoregressive Text-to-Image Models
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Jilin University, Tsinghua University - Tsinghua Shenzhen International Graduate School, South China University of Technology, Harbin Industry University and Tsinghua University - Tsinghua Shenzhen International Graduate School

detail.title: JailAR: Evaluating the Jailbreak Vulnerability of Visual Autoregressive Text-to-Image Models
detail.abstract: Recent advances in visual autoregressive models (VARs) enable text-to-image generation rivaling or surpassing diffusion-based methods. However, the security risks of VARs, including jailbreak attacks, remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we present the first comprehensive study of jailbreak vulnerabilities in visual autoregressive models. We transfer six representative jailbreak attack strategies originally designed for diffusion models to the autoregressive setting and evaluate their effectiveness. These attacks exhibit varied performance in the VAR setting and show substantial differences compared to their behavior in diffusion models. Furthermore, we examine two widely adopted defense mechanisms, namely safety filter and unsafe concept erasure, to assess their robustness under these attacks. Our experimental results reveal that visual autoregressive models are highly susceptible to jailbreak attacks, often exhibiting failure modes comparable to or more severe than those observed in diffusion models. Moreover, we find that existing defenses provide limited protection and can be readily bypassed. Motivated by these findings, we propose a novel plug-and-play defense mechanism that significantly reduces jailbreak success rates without requiring model retraining. Our study highlights fundamental security vulnerabilities in VARs generation and underscores the urgent need for principled defense strategies tailored to this emerging model class.

title: A Practical Implementation of Differential Privacy for Customer Review Analytics in E-Business: Balancing Utility and PDPL Compliance
affiliations: King Saud University and King Saud University

detail.title: A Practical Implementation of Differential Privacy for Customer Review Analytics in E-Business: Balancing Utility and PDPL Compliance
detail.abstract: Customer review analytics are becoming an important part of the e-business platform to aggregate product ratings, analyze sentiment, and provide personalized recommendations. Nonetheless, such analytics are a big threat to privacy since the individual reviews can have implicit personal data that can be traced to users. The Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) in Saudi Arabia obliges the anonymization of personal data before any processing in the country, but conventional methods of anonymization have been susceptible to re identification attacks. Differential privacy (DP) provides a mathematically-rigid model of anonymizing aggregate statistics with an analysis utility. The paper is the practical implementation of the differential privacy of customer review analytics based on the Laplace and Exponential mechanisms. The application is tested against the Yelp Open Dataset which consists of 6.7 million customer reviews in real world. A systematic evaluation of privacy-utility tradeoff is done in privacy budgets ε = {0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10. Findings show that when the values of the three parameters are ϵ = 1, the relative error in the average rating queries is less than 5.5 percent, a tolerable amount in most e-business decision scenarios. Moreover, a direct correspondence between DP guarantees and the standard of not reasonably identifiable of PDPL is given, whereby, an approximation value of 1 is suggested as a viable compliance value. The entire source code and a non-obligatory interactive dashboard are open-sourced in order to enable e-business adoption and additional studies.

title: Agentic AI and Airline Pricing: Demand Cliffs, Elasticity Migration, and the Fate of Fare Fencing under Delegated Booking
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University

detail.title: Agentic AI and Airline Pricing: Demand Cliffs, Elasticity Migration, and the Fate of Fare Fencing under Delegated Booking
detail.abstract: Autonomous AI agents that search, compare, and book flights on travelers' behalf are moving from demonstration to deployment, while airline pricing theory largely presumes a human buyer. This paper develops a formal framework for airline markets in which the buyer is an algorithm. A traveler's booking instruction is modeled as a machine-readable delegation contract, comprising a budget cap, a departure window, a preferred carrier with a switching threshold, and a patience budget, executed by the agent as a deterministic threshold policy. A population of contracts then induces a demand function equal to the survival function of the budget-cap distribution, a step-like schedule that inherits the atoms of the cap distribution as demand cliffs and renders drip pricing allocatively inert. Deterministic simulation experiments trace the consequences through a mixed human, agent market as agent penetration rises. Price sensitivity migrates from the whole fare range to a small set of contract thresholds, a shift summarized by an elasticity concentration index. The optimal posted fare comes to shadow the cap atoms, reaching them through a discrete jump or a gradual creep depending on their position relative to the human optimum, and remaining pinned thereafter. Maximized profit rises with penetration when stated caps track valuations and falls when caps sit below them. Intertemporal fare fencing loses its premium as delegation severs the correlation between purchase timing and valuation, surviving only where the joint distribution of contract parameters reconstructs it. Implications for revenue management, loyalty programs, and distribution strategy are discussed.

title: Systemic Risk, Recommender Systems and Content Governance: The Digital Services Act and the Reinvention of Platform Regulation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Systemic Risk, Recommender Systems and Content Governance: The Digital Services Act and the Reinvention of Platform Regulation
detail.abstract: the European Union's 2022/2065 concerning a Unified Market for Services on the Internet (the ’Digital Services in Academic Domains Act’ or ’DSA’) represents the most audacious European endeavor thus far to transcend the two-decade framework established by the Internet Commerce Directive and thereby redefine online intermediaries as proactive shapers of the online public sphere. This article examines the DSA's hierarchical framework of responsibilities, its preferential approach toward extremely large online spaces and search engines via the notion of 'systemic risk', its governance of machine learning recommendation systems and deceptive practices, and the nascent enactment actions of the European Commission, which is operating as a primary internet oversight body for the very first time. It argues that the DSA represents a fundamental rather than a gradual change in European platforms management, and its enduring significance will rely on how Articles 34 and 35 are practically interpreted by the Commission, the judiciary, and the appointed agencies. A formal segment establishes mathematical framework connecting the dynamics of recommended systems, virality thresholds, and the evaluation of systemic risk. The document concludes with five reformation objectives for the subsequent execution phase involving the DSA.

detail.abstract: Platform governance shapes not only how value is created in digital ecosystems but also who is better positioned to create it. Yet little is known about how governance interventions triggered by external pressures affect value creation across platform privilege structures. We investigate a bitrate restriction on Twitch, a global livestreaming platform, in South Korea. Implemented in response to rising network fees, this governance intervention constrained  streamers’ access to a critical operational resource. We find that the intervention reduced streamer value creation, measured by average concurrent viewership, by approximately 9.6%. This harm was unevenly distributed, concentrating among the least-privileged streamers, while more-privileged streamers appeared partially buffered by platform-endowed technical resources and their established audience bases. Streamers reconfigured their content portfolios in response, but the performance implications of this adaptation depend on its form and platform privilege. We theorize and empirically show how resource-restricting governance interventions produce governance-induced digital inequality and condition participant adaptation in platform ecosystems.

title: Design of Collaborative Control Algorithms for Edge Computing-Enabled Distributed Computing Nodes
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Design of Collaborative Control Algorithms for Edge Computing-Enabled Distributed Computing Nodes
detail.abstract: To address scheduling failures caused by heterogeneous computing power, limited communication bandwidth, and dynamic topology changes in edge computing networks, this paper proposes an adaptive collaborative management algorithm for distributed computer nodes enabled by edge computing. This research constructs a decentralized resource peer-to-peer scheduling engine by coupling a lightweight state-space prediction mechanism with multi-objective offloading cost optimization, reducing the probability of communication congestion caused by high-frequency global state synchronization. To address network link interference from external signal-to-noise ratio factors, a finite-time consensus protocol based on Laplace gradients is introduced to maintain the convergence stability of the distributed node decision update process. Multi-dimensional performance tests based on physical edge clusters and simulation frameworks show that, under conditions of high concurrency in task arrival and random node failures, the algorithm can maintain a system throughput of over 90% and control the end-to-end average latency within a reasonable range. Compared to traditional heuristic greedy algorithms and hash mapping baselines, it exhibits more stable computational energy efficiency, providing theoretical support for large-scale networking of heterogeneous industrial IoT.

detail.abstract: As universities respond to rapid digital transformation, the challenge extends beyond adopting new technologies to building systems that strengthen governance, improve institutional performance and prepare people to lead in an increasingly data-driven world. This paper examines Nnamdi Azikiwe University (NAU), Nigeria, as a case of institution-led digital transformation centred on the Central Information Referencing and Management System (CIRMS). Developed and owned by the University, CIRMS integrates key academic and administrative functions, including student and staff records, performance appraisal, financial operations and institutional reporting. Situated within a wider ecosystem of e-learning, digital credential verification, research resources and emerging artificial intelligence-enabled platforms, CIRMS illustrates NAU's transition from fragmented administrative processes towards integrated institutional intelligence. Drawing on the University's implementation experience, the paper examines how this evolving digital architecture supports administrative efficiency, data integrity, transparency, accountability and evidenceinformed decision-making, while strengthening the digital competencies required for future leadership. It further identifies institutional ownership, local technical capacity, interoperability and adaptability as important foundations for sustainable digital transformation. We present the NAU experience as an emerging framework through which locally developed digital systems can connect institutional governance with talent development and future-ready leadership. The experience offers practical lessons for higher education institutions, particularly in the Global South, seeking context-responsive and sustainable approaches to digital transformation while retaining ownership of their institutional data, systems and capabilities.

detail.abstract: This study explores Quantum-Native Organisational Design (QNOD) and its impact on agility, innovation performance, and competitive advantage among 384 firms in South Africa. The concept of QNOD is operationally defined through the application of Structural Equation Modelling using Analysis of Moment Structures (AMOS) in the form of three dimensions: strategic superposition, structural fluidity, and quantum talent density. Results show that quantum-native organisations are more adaptable, have better innovative performance and possess improved competitive advantage than conventional organisations. Organisational agility plays a mediating role between QNOD and innovative performance, whereas quantum-native design also positively impacts competitive advantage directly. These findings reveal QNOD as a quantifiable and performance-augmenting organisational structure that boosts adaptability, innovation, and competitiveness, either directly or through agility. Moreover, it provides managers with a tangible roadmap of strategic superposition, structural fluidity, and quantum talent density for reorganising organisations under dynamic conditions.

Because, it equips one with knowledge and skills to enhance a better future.  On the contrary, legal education makes people aware of their rights, responsibilities, and how the justice system works. title: Vicarious Liability In Idaho Under Jones: Examining Idaho's Expanded Liability After Nearly Two Decades

detail.abstract: Under the common law, vicarious liability extended tort liability to employers when an employee committed a tort within the scope of their employment. Since then, developments in both tort and agency law have expanded the imputation of tort liability beyond the traditional employer-employee relationship, ultimately capturing principals, agents, and independent contractors. In 2006, the American Law Institute published the Restatement (Third) of Agency, which offered the single greatest expansion within vicarious liability jurisprudence. Under section 7.08 of the Restatement (Third), a principal may be held vicariously liable for the actions or communications of an agent, so long as the injured party reasonably believed that the agent acted with apparent authority. Previously, section 267 of the Restatement (Second) required the plaintiff to show a detrimental change of position in reliance on the manifestations of an agent in order impute liability. In 2009, Idaho became one of the first states to adopt section 7.08's expansive view of vicarious liability in Jones v. HealthSouth Treasure Valley Hospital. As the twentieth anniversary of Jones approaches, the aim of this paper is to investigate the evolution of vicarious liability jurisprudence, detail the adoption of that evolution in Idaho, and inform the discussion as to whether Jones should be revisited by the Idaho Supreme Court or the Idaho Legislature.

title: Ending the Adverse Possession of Authorship
affiliations: Samford University - Cumberland School of Law

detail.title: Ending the Adverse Possession of Authorship

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.funderStatement: No topic-specific funding. My university employer pays me a salary and stipend for which research like this is part of my job.

detail.abstract:
This is the first article to cohesively identify, analyze, and argue against a pernicious doctrine within U.S. copyright law: the adverse possession of authorship. Its tendrils have spread through three decades of case law, effectively stripping people of their legal status as authors and shifting it to others who did not create what they did.

The doctrine functions as follows: if you do not sue to assert your authorship soon enough after someone repudiates it, you lose it. So if, for example, you write a song with someone who later insists he wrote the whole thing alone, you have three years under the Copyright Act’s statute of limitations to challenge him in court. Wait a day more, and your authorship is effectively adversely possessed. Your collaborator is now, as a legal matter, the song’s sole author.

This is both atextual and myopic. It is atextual in that the statute of limitations bars untimely claims, but authorship is not a claim; authorship is a status, one stemming solely from the act of creation. It is myopic in that authorship has an overarching, immutable function in copyright law. Authorship controls who initially owns a copyright. Authorship dictates whether and how transfers of ownership can be terminated. Authorship governs how long a copyright will last. And, as the advent of generative artificial intelligence has starkly shown, authorship determines whether a copyright exists at all.

Accordingly, although a given claim can be untimely—such as one for profits not shared with you prior to the three years leading up to your suit—authorship should remain inviolate, regardless of whether and when someone else repudiates it. Simply put, the adverse possession of authorship should cease. The Constitution itself may demand it.

But practical conundrums abound. Absent adverse possession, there is no brightline time limit on any authorship dispute. The later that courts can hear such disputes, the more they will have to deal with faded memories, lost documents, and dead authors’ estates, and the greater the risk that their rulings will disturb dealings long thought settled. Moreover, for every belated but meritorious assertion of authorship, at least as many may be unscrupulous money-grabs.

This Article aims, then, to offer other paths forward while minding the practical pitfalls. Along the way, broadly useful insights into authorship, and its vexing relationship with time, will be revealed.

detail.abstract: GLP-1 usage has fundamentally altered the foods that consumers buy and are sold through retail stores. In this paper, we study the strategic effects of food manufacturers' responses to GLP-1-driven changes in consumption. We find that product design facilitates greater protein demand from shoppers, and equilibrium prices are substantially higher than in the pre-reformulation equilibrium, but consumer welfare is dramatically higher when firms reformulate in response to higher demand for GLP-1 friendly food products. Strategic reformulation alone can justify a far larger public investment in GLP-1 medication subsidies than previously believed.

detail.abstract: While one is negotiating for a particular property, another person often enters the process with a more attractive bid, snatching the property away from the first party. In the Talmud, this is known as "ani hamehapech bechararah" (literally, "If a poor person is engaging in the acquisition of a cake"), and, according to Jewish law, the second party is considered wicked ("rasha"). This topic matters because it shows how Jewish law reaches beyond what strict legal rules require, pressing individuals toward lifnim mishurat hadin, conduct that goes beyond the letter of the law. By branding a legally permissible act as wicked, the Talmud demonstrates that halacha (Jewish law) is designed to cultivate character and communal ethics, not merely to police outright theft or fraud. This paper examines the implications of this law in the realm of commerce, dating, and finding employment, and contrasts it with American tort law's treatment of interference with prospective economic relations, where the same conduct is generally protected as legitimate competition.

detail.abstract:
This report presents the first comprehensive analysis of zoning in the fourteen-county Kansas City metropolitan area, including Bates, Caldwell, Cass, Clay, Clinton, Jackson, Johnson, Lafayette, Leavenworth, Linn, Miami, Platte, Ray, and Wyandotte Counties. It illuminates a fragmented regulatory landscape that limits housing access and economic opportunity, while corresponding with high levels of racial and economic segregation. By exposing these issues, this report underscores the urgency of regionwide zoning reform on both sides of State Line Road, and provides a roadmap for policymakers and advocates on how to get there.

A first-of-its-kind dataset built by the National Zoning Atlas (NZA) enables people to compare zoning codes across places and determine the extent to which zoning rules across the region restrict or allow housing, and whether zoning rules reinforce the racial segregation goals of years past. 

Part I begins this report by exploring the region’s housing challenges, the two-state governance structure that shapes its zoning, and an overview of how zoning works.

Part II describes the NZA’s methodology for analyzing and digitizing zoning codes. This methodology enables data collection at an unprecedented scale, increasing public understanding of zoning through accessible visualizations and evidence-based analysis.

Part III details five key findings about zoning conditions across the Kansas City metro today:  
  • Only 3% of the region’s residentially zoned land allows apartments by right.
  • Most single-family land requires homes to sit on lots of nearly two acres.
  • One-third of single-family land bans accessory dwelling units.
  • 99% of residentially zoned land carries a parking mandate.
  • In the region’s urban and suburban core, the most exclusionary zoning is
  • concentrated in the Whitest, wealthiest neighborhoods.

Part IV combines NZA zoning data with census data to examine how, in the region’s urban and suburban core, the most restrictive rules map onto race and income at the neighborhood level. It traces how a system built on explicit racial exclusion was converted into one of durable economic exclusion.

Part V concludes with five actionable recommendations for policymakers on both sides of the state line to expand housing choice, lower costs, and build communities that better reflect the needs and desires of today’s residents.

title: Chlorine Dioxide-Driven Oxidation of In-Service Polyethylene Pipes in Potable Water Distribution Networks
affiliations: Hamad Bin Khalifa University, RWTH Aachen University and Hamad Bin Khalifa University - Qatar Environment and Energy Research Institute

detail.title: Chlorine Dioxide-Driven Oxidation of In-Service Polyethylene Pipes in Potable Water Distribution Networks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts stated
declarations.funderStatement: This research was made possible by the Graduate Sponsorship Research Award (GSRA11-L-2-0609-24111) from the Qatar National Research Fund, an office of Qatar Research, Development and Innovation Council (QRDI), a member of the Qatar Foundation

detail.abstract:
High-density polyethylene (HDPE) pipes are widely used in drinking water distribution networks, yet disinfectants can promote long-term oxidation and embrittlement of polymers, especially under chlorine dioxide (ClO2) residuals. Most prior studies rely on accelerated tests, and it remains unclear to what extent realistic, spatially varying disinfectant residuals lead to measurable degradation under service conditions. In this study, HDPE pipes retrieved after 2, 4.5, 5, and 6 years of service in ClO2-disinfected potable water networks were evaluated alongside laboratory-aged specimens exposed at 30 °C to low and high residual conditions (≈ 0.04 and 2 mg/L ClO2). FTIR and XPS analysis were conducted to assess surface chemistry and quantify oxidation products, and SEM/EDS was used to identify deposit layers and damage morphology. Oxidation-induction time (OIT) assessed oxidative stability, and hardness testing compared the inner pipe surface to the cross-section to evaluate near-surface hardness variation. In the laboratory series, the carbonyl index remained essentially unchanged under low ClO₂ conditions over 10 weeks, whereas at high residual conditions, a carbonyl feature emerged around week 6 and increased by week 10. XPS indicated the presence of highly oxidized surface groups (O-C=O) on high-residual conditions and the field pipes. SEM observations shifted from deposit-masked surface containing aluminosilicate layers (2-year pipe) to crack-dominated morphologies (older field pipes). OIT decreased from 45.7 (virgin HDPE) to 29.6 min (2-year) and reached a minimum of 4.3 min (4.5-year). Hardness differences were small in the laboratory-aged samples, while field samples showed larger inner diameter to cross-section increase, with the maximum difference of 1.04 HBW. In non-ClO₂-exposed samples, bottled-water bioassays, minimal microbial response was observed, with the strongest response during the early cycles. While TOC increased substantially in the ClO₂ batch due to the carbon in the disinfectant tablet, minimal differences between the samples and negative controls were observed.

Overall, the combined chemical, thermal, and mechanical results indicate that oxidation and mechanical degradation under ClO2 are strongly location-dependent. Field pipes exhibited the most distinct ID-localized oxidative features consistent with a shift toward mechanically vulnerable surfaces under realistic network conditions. Under the tested conditions, virgin HDPE produced only a limited and transient microbial regrowth response.

title: Uncertainty Shocks, Investor Sentiment, and Hedging Performance: Evidence from Taiwan’s Options Market
affiliations: National Kaohsiung University of Science and Technology and National Kaohsiung University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Uncertainty Shocks, Investor Sentiment, and Hedging Performance: Evidence from Taiwan’s Options Market
detail.abstract: This study examines how market sentiment and different forms of uncertainty are transmitted into volatility expectations and hedging outcomes in Taiwan’s options market. Using daily data on TAIEX options from 2012 to 2021, we compare the informational content of stock sentiment, option sentiment, and uncertainty measures for implied volatility and delta-hedging performance. The results show that the volatility index (VIX), infectious disease equity market volatility (EMV), and Twitter-based economic uncertainty (TEU) exhibit the strongest volatility-forecasting performance. For hedging outcomes, the economic value of uncertainty measures varies across option characteristics, with TEU providing relatively strong improvements in several specifications. We also document asymmetric effects of sentiment and uncertainty across market conditions. The relatively strong performance of social-media-based uncertainty suggests that the channel through which uncertainty information is disseminated matters for volatility expectations and risk management. In Taiwan’s retail-intensive derivatives market, rapidly transmitted information may be particularly relevant to investor behavior and hedging outcomes. Overall, the findings highlight the joint importance of information channels and market structure in shaping the transmission of uncertainty into derivatives-market risk management.

title: Heat
affiliations: Albany Law School and Albany Law School

detail.title: Heat

declarations.declarationOfInterest: not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: not applicable

detail.abstract: Heat is changing how we are born, how we live, and how we die. Temperatures are rising and heat is our new normal. This is the unescapable – often stifling –  reality for 21st century existence. Despite the fact that heat kills more people than any other climate hazard, it remains under-examined in the legal literature. This Article seeks to correct that omission by offering one of the first sustained treatments of heat as a distinct and urgent problem for law and policy. It begins by grounding readers in the science of a warming planet, explaining why rising temperatures are inevitable even as the suffering from rising temperatures cause is not. From there, the Article builds a granular, intersectional taxonomy of heat vulnerability to examine how heat uniquely endangers pregnant people, the elderly, domestic violence survivors, unhoused populations, outdoor workers, disaster-displaced migrants, athletes, pets, and even the physical infrastructure and everyday objects society depends on. Each vulnerability is examined not as an isolated data point but as evidence that heat operates as a threat multiplier, compounding existing patterns of poverty, race, disability, gender, and geography. The Article then turns from diagnosis to prescription, surveying federal retrenchment and emerging state and local innovation, from California's equity-driven heat action plans to hydration stations, cooling corridors, and heat-resilient land use planning, to explore what serious legal engagement with heat could look like. The Article concludes with an invocation for more collective thinking and iterative learning around legal and political responses to heat in order to address one of this generation’s most pervasive threats to human health and well-being.

title: Occupancy-Based Network Reduction for Recursive-Logit Route-Choice Estimation
affiliations: School of Computing and Information Systems and Phenikaa University

detail.title: Occupancy-Based Network Reduction for Recursive-Logit Route-Choice Estimation
detail.abstract: Recursive logit (RL) is a fundamental and behaviorally appealing route-choice model that represents a complete route as a sequence of link-level decisions, allowing choice probabilities to be defined over the full set of feasible paths without requiring explicit path enumeration. However, maximum-likelihood estimation repeatedly solves destination-conditioned value systems on the full network, which can be costly and numerically fragile on large cyclic graphs. We propose occupancy-based network reduction to accelerate RL estimation and improve its numerical robustness. For each origin--destination pair, link relevance is measured by the expected number of traversals before first arrival at the absorbing destination. Maximizing occupancy over plausible utility parameters avoids reliance on a single coefficient vector. Links with negligible occupancy are removed, while observed-route and connectivity links are retained; similar reduced networks are grouped and cached. The resulting estimator preserves the conventional RL likelihood on a smaller, behaviorally relevant network.We establish approximation guarantees connecting the occupancy threshold to excluded-route probability, total-variation distance, and retained-route likelihood error. Under feature-moment and curvature conditions, the threshold also controls gradient and coefficient errors. Synthetic, semi-synthetic, and observed-data experiments on the Borlange and GeoLife networks show that the reduced estimator closely reproduces full-network likelihoods and coefficients. The largest synthetic experiment yields a 160-fold cached-estimation speedup, while real-data gains depend on the amount of behaviorally irrelevant structure in the reference network. Stress tests further show that removing low-occupancy cycles can enlarge the numerically evaluable parameter region. Overall, occupancy-based network reduction provides a faster and more numerically robust approach to RL estimation, with explicit approximation guarantees and diagnostics for when network expansion is required.

title: From Stakeholder Pressure and Carbon Anxiety to Twin Transformation
affiliations: National Taiwan University of Science and Technology, Tamkang University, National Taiwan Normal University, Masaryk University and Technical University of Liberec

detail.title: From Stakeholder Pressure and Carbon Anxiety to Twin Transformation
detail.abstract: Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory, this study conceptualizes stakeholder pressure and carbon anxiety as sensing triggers, green digital transformation capability and investment in sustainability training as seizing mechanisms, and twin transformation as a reconfiguring outcome. Survey data were collected from 173 manufacturing companies in Taiwan, and structural equation modeling was employed to test the proposed research model. The results show that nearly all hypotheses were supported, except for the positive effect of carbon anxiety on green digital transformation capability. Moreover, investment in sustainability training was found to mediate the relationship between carbon anxiety and twin transformation

title: Connecting Firms, Shaping Jobs: Shared Analysts and Corporate Hiring
affiliations: Wenzhou Business College, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Macau - Faculty of Business Administration

detail.title: Connecting Firms, Shaping Jobs: Shared Analysts and Corporate Hiring
detail.abstract: This study examines whether shared financial analyst coverage shapes firms’ hiring decisions. Using text-based measures of online job postings and an exhaustive sample of same-industry, same-year firm pairs in China, we find that firms connected through common analysts exhibit significantly greater similarity in subsequent hiring profiles. The effect is evident across technical, functional, sales, engineering, and finance positions. The results are robust to analyses of analyst-network formation and exit, alternative variable definitions, and matching-based specifications, consistent with an information-spillover channel. The association between shared analyst coverage and hiring similarity is negative when common analysts have greater research output or are affiliated with star brokers, consistent with more capable analysts providing customized, firm-specific advice rather than encouraging imitation. Further analyses show that hiring similarity is associated with higher productivity but lower patenting activity. Our findings extend the literature on analyst networks by showing that capital-market information spillovers influence firms’ human-capital decisions.

title: Is Gold a Safe Haven? Crisis-Specific and Long-Run Evidence from Return Correlations in India
affiliations: Ranchi University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Is Gold a Safe Haven? Crisis-Specific and Long-Run Evidence from Return Correlations in India
detail.abstract: This study analyses whether gold acts as a hedge or safe haven for the Indian stock market using long-run and crisis-specific return-based methods. Monthly data from 2008–2025 and daily data for the Global Financial Crisis, COVID-19, and the Russia–Ukraine war are used to estimate Pearson and Spearman correlations between gold and Nifty returns, with 60, 120, and 240-day windows. Results show moderate negative long-run correlation, indicating partial hedging, while safe-haven behaviour varies across crises and is strongest during the Russia–Ukraine war, highlighting time-varying diversification benefits.

title: Techno-Economic Viability of Small Modular Reactors for Behind-the-Meter Data-Centre Power Provision in Sub-Saharan Africa
affiliations: Xi'an Jiaotong University, , affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Techno-Economic Viability of Small Modular Reactors for Behind-the-Meter Data-Centre Power Provision in Sub-Saharan Africa
detail.abstract: This study presents the first techno-economic assessment of small modular reactors (SMRs) powering data centres behind the meter in Sub-Saharan Africa, addressing a critical gap where rising digital infrastructure demand collides with unreliable grids and costly polluting diesel dependency. Using a Mixed-Integer Quadratic Program (MIQP) to optimise the hourly dispatch and sizing of the reactors against the data centre, we found that at a central 12% discount rate, every facility is economically viable against a $300/MWhe diesel benchmark, with a median breakeven of approximately $206/MWhe. Viability survives adverse capital cost or adverse financing, but not both together, implying capital cost containment and cheap finance are the two levers. Viability is governed by facility scale rather than per country. The optimal reactor class shifts endogenously with load, and the largest facilities exhibit both the lowest breakeven prices and the greatest resilience to adverse financing. Across 37 candidate facilities above 2 MW, viability persists from optimistic (5%) to realistic (12%) discount rates and degrades only when high capital cost and high financing (interest rate) cost coincide. The viable fleet avoids on the order of 13 Mt of CO2 per year relative to diesel, concentrated in South Africa. These results further show that the near-term opportunity for SMR-powered data centres lie at hyperscale campuses, while clustered multi-facility configurations remain an important topic for future investigation.

title: Traceable Decision Support for Grid-Scale Battery Storage: Integrating Cost, Carbon, Circularity and Deployment Portfolios
affiliations: and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Traceable Decision Support for Grid-Scale Battery Storage: Integrating Cost, Carbon, Circularity and Deployment Portfolios
detail.abstract: Grid-scale battery procurement requires defensible comparisons that integrate economic performance, environmental burdens, material security and deployment readiness. This study develops an evidence-governed decision-support framework combining techno-economic assessment, delivered-energy life-cycle carbon accounting, a disclosed circularity indicator, grouped machine-learning diagnostics, complementary multi-criteria rankings and illustrative portfolio allocation. The analysis-ready dataset contains 384 traceable cases spanning two storage technologies, six grid services, four regions, four deployment scenarios and two bounded parameter draws. Across all cases, lithium iron phosphate systems average 83.3 USD MWh⁻¹ and 41.8 kg CO₂e MWh⁻¹, compared with 87.8 USD MWh⁻¹ and 54.6 kg CO₂e MWh⁻¹ for sodium-ion systems. Sodium-ion nevertheless achieves lower modeled costs under the 2030 and 2035 learning scenarios and exhibits lower critical-material risk. Grouped cross-validation yields random-forest R² values of 0.963, 0.912 and 0.974 for levelized cost, life-cycle emissions and ranking score, respectively; however, linear baselines outperform the forest for the latter two targets. TOPSIS and VIKOR show broad rank association but share only three of their ten highest-ranked alternatives, underscoring decision-rule sensitivity. An illustrative 12-project allocation combines seven sodium-ion and five incumbent projects, totaling 1,480 MWh and 174.9 million USD under a non-binding budget ceiling. These findings support conditional, service-specific diversification rather than technology-universal superiority and establish explicit boundaries for downstream reproducibility.

title: From the K2 Mountain to the Titan Submersible: Translating the Deep Structure of Experiential Management Simulations
affiliations: Cranfield University and Cranfield University - School of Management

detail.title: From the K2 Mountain to the Titan Submersible: Translating the Deep Structure of Experiential Management Simulations
detail.abstract: Experiential simulations can create powerful management learning, yet adapting a successful simulation to a new context risks preserving its visible features while losing the mechanisms that generated learning. This conceptual article examines how simulation-based pedagogy can evolve through deliberate translation rather than replication. Using a retrospective, theory-informed design reconstruction, we compare the development of the K2 simulation with the instructional architecture of the Titan Submersible Challenge. Building on the development and repeated delivery of K2, we examine how its underlying learning mechanisms informed a second-generation simulation for teaching complexity, adaptive judgment, and leadership. We introduce the Deep-Structure Simulation Translation framework, comprising six connected design moves: distilling generative mechanisms; re-anchoring authentic tension; encoding theory in mechanics; distributing knowledge and agency; disrupting within a holding environment; and debriefing, reconnecting, and iterating. We argue that simulation translation depends on maintaining alignment between intended learning and the mechanisms through which participants experience uncertainty, interdependence, constrained resources, competing priorities, and consequential choice. The analysis generates five propositions for future empirical examination. The framework shifts attention from simulation as an engaging representation of a case toward simulation as a deliberately designed architecture for learning and offers management educators a theoretically grounded approach for adaptation across contexts.

title: Certified envelopes for day-ahead cooling-side flexibility from liquid-cooled AI data-center thermal inertia in electricity markets
affiliations: University of Houston and Miami University

detail.title: Certified envelopes for day-ahead cooling-side flexibility from liquid-cooled AI data-center thermal inertia in electricity markets
detail.abstract: Artificial-intelligence computing is adding gigawatts of load to grids that now condition interconnection on flexibility. A liquid-cooled hall supplies it by letting its coolant warm, which cuts chiller power. Selling those cuts a day ahead is hard for two reasons. How deep a cut it can promise moves with tomorrow's humidity and workload, and a priced shortfall differs from a chip running too hot, which nothing pays for. This paper proposes ENCORE, Envelope-Certified Offering and Recourse. It computes the set of deliverable cuts, a polyhedron whose right-hand side moves with the dew-point forecast, then shrinks it by the worst case two calibrated disturbance sets admit, a wide one for chip safety and a narrow one for priced delivery, each calibrated per hour-of-day block at a level that tracks misses. A fixed-gain controller then delivers the offer, and on every hour the certificate covers it holds the chips safe and meets the metered whole-hour obligation. Across ten 2024 ERCOT weeks, on a causal price forecast and a stylized 30-minute reserve product, the hall commits 127 kW-h/day per megawatt of information-technology load and returns $7.45/MW-day with no hotspot violation on any covered hour, against an uncertified envelope that breaches the limit on 227 of 1,400 replayed day-and-seed combinations. Declaring an hour unavailable when its realized start sits outside the certified set turns down 104 of 190 calls and removes every failure and episode. No certificate break appears in four climates spanning 20 K of mean dew point, or across campuses of up to twenty halls.

title: The Omega Block: Correlation-Network Features that Improve Systemic Tail-Loss Attribution Beyond Downside Beta and Conditional MES

detail.title: The Omega Block: Correlation-Network Features that Improve Systemic Tail-Loss Attribution Beyond Downside Beta and Conditional MES
detail.abstract: Attributing future systemic tail losses across assets remains dominated by exposures estimated asset by asset, market beta, downside beta and volatility, although drawdowns are precisely the episodes in which losses become collective and concentrate where shocks recirculate among tightly co-moving names. The quantities proposed here originate in our prior work on network fragility: the FSRI, a structural index for microbial co-occurrence networks in agricultural soils, and its financial descendant, the TSI, whose standalone version we falsified and reported. From that starting point we hypothesized that the same structural information could carry marginal value if localized to individual assets, extended with a response dimension, and handed to a flexible learner as features rather than composed by hand. The result is the Omega Block: five per-asset features computed from daily prices alone, two triadic quantities measured against a closed-form configuration null and three response quantities around scheduled FOMC announcements, among them Omega-R, a perturbation response normalized by each asset's own baseline drift, developed for this block. In pre-registered paired ablations with a same-width noise placebo, the block adds 1.3 to 3.4 points of out-of-fold R 2 to next-year tail-loss attribution over baselines that instantiate the public state of the art, up to 31 columns including sector, downside beta, co-moments, a conditional MES proxy, size, liquidity and balance-sheet fundamentals, replicated on two universes and two nearly disjoint periods (2012-2017, 2016-2025), while the placebo worsens the same model in every configuration. Because the baselines that decide adoption in practice are proprietary, the paper's verification is designed to travel to the data: an open acceptance harness reruns the entire protocol on any universe, baseline and event calendar, with a values-only mode and a cryptographic time-lock. The scope established by the evidence is cross-sectional attribution, not market timing.

title: When Scientific Comment Becomes Public Accusation
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: When Scientific Comment Becomes Public Accusation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial relationship with PubPeer, any named commenter, any media outlet discussed, or any publisher cited.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this article.

detail.abstract: This article examines PubPeer as a website for post-publication comments and asks when scientific criticism becomes public accusation. It deliberately does not rank commenters or infer the identities of pseudonymous accounts; those questions require a separate account-level method. The analysis instead tests the platform’s rules, moderation design, permanence, author-response structure and external integrations against a critical-discourse model of reputational power. Five escalation mechanisms are identified: replacing an observable feature with a culpability label; attributing intention; expanding one concern into a verdict on a person or field; using contempt to narrow the space for reply; and demanding sanction before independent review. PubPeer forbids misconduct allegations, personal comments, motive speculation and hyperbole, but it also disclaims scientific review, ordinarily retains threads after an author response or journal action, and gives readers responsibility for judging accuracy. Once PubPeer links are surfaced in publisher screening and bibliographic databases, that combination is not neutral infrastructure. It can make visibility resemble verification and repetition resemble corroboration. The article proposes a mandatory separation between observation, inference, allegation and adjudication; universal language moderation; evidence-location requirements; verified notice; state-labelled replies and resolutions; independent appeal; equal-prominence correction; and a prohibition on adverse institutional action based only on a PubPeer link. The ethical demand is direct: a platform that distributes suspicion must also distribute uncertainty, response and correction with equal force.

title: An Integrative Conceptual Framework for Emotional Safety, Attachment, Communication, and Relationship Quality
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: An Integrative Conceptual Framework for Emotional Safety, Attachment, Communication, and Relationship Quality

declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this conceptual paper, as the research did not involve human participants, patient data, personal data collection, clinical intervention, or experimental procedures.

detail.abstract:
Relationship Intelligence (RI) is proposed as an integrative conceptual framework for understanding how individuals perceive, interpret, regulate, communicate, and respond to relational information within intimate relationships. Drawing on established research in adult attachment, emotion regulation, perceived partner responsiveness, intimacy, interpersonal communication, conflict processes, commitment, and relationship quality, this paper examines how these traditionally distinct psychological processes may operate together as a coordinated relational capacity.

The framework proposes six interrelated dimensions of Relationship Intelligence: Relational Self-Awareness; Partner Attunement and Perspective-Taking; Emotional Regulation; Relational Communication; Conflict Navigation and Repair; and Emotional Safety and Responsive Connection. It further introduces the Relationship Intelligence Arc™, a recursive relational-processing model comprising eight stages: Notice, Understand Self, Attune, Regulate, Communicate, Navigate, Repair, and Integrate.

Three additional concepts—Interactional Metacognition, Responsive Calibration, and Relational Coordination—are proposed to explain how individuals recognize recurring dyadic patterns, adjust responses according to their interpersonal impact, and coordinate multiple relational capacities over time.

The paper also presents a preliminary Relationship Intelligence Scale (RIS) item framework and outlines a research agenda for construct development, psychometric validation, dyadic testing, longitudinal investigation, cross-cultural validation, and intervention research. Relationship Intelligence is presented as a proposed conceptual and research framework requiring empirical validation, rather than as an established psychological theory, validated intelligence construct, diagnostic instrument, or clinically validated intervention.

title: Mapping the technological evolution trajectory of intelligent drilling: A full-text mining knowledge graph framework integrating large language models and GraphRAG
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Mapping the technological evolution trajectory of intelligent drilling: A full-text mining knowledge graph framework integrating large language models and GraphRAG
detail.abstract: In the context of the global low-carbon energy transformation, improving upstream exploration production efficiency and reducing carbon footprint have become key needs, and intelligent drilling is a key technological solution. However, the rapid expansion of intelligent drilling research has generated a large amount of fragmented literature, making it difficult to systematically organize technological associations and predict low-carbon, digital development paths using traditional review and retrieval methods. This paper proposes an integrated intelligent drilling knowledge mining framework that combines bibliometric analysis, large language model (LLM)-driven efficient text extraction, and Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG). Based on a literature corpus retrieved from the Web of Science, quantitative bibliometric analysis is first performed to graph the overall research landscape. Then, using structured validity statements extracted by LLM, a domain knowledge graph with 1-3-hop inference capabilities is constructed to capture the complex relationships between technology, equipment, and engineering objectives. A high‐precision professional question‐answering (QA) system is further developed to alleviate LLM hallucinations in energy scenarios. Finally, knowledge graph topology analysis and evolutionary pattern mining are applied to predict the long-term technology trajectory of intelligent drilling. The results verify that the proposed framework provides reliable support for domain knowledge organization and provides data-driven reference for the low-carbon and digital transformation of oil and gas drilling operations.

title: The Reverse Flynn Effect in the Digital Age: Comprehensive Theoretical Framework, Future Scenarios, and Evidence-Based Solutions
affiliations: Al-Neelain University - Department of Economics

detail.title: The Reverse Flynn Effect in the Digital Age: Comprehensive Theoretical Framework, Future Scenarios, and Evidence-Based Solutions

detail.abstract: The twenty-first century has witnessed an unprecedented reversal of the historical Flynn Effect, with cognitive performance declining across multiple developed nations, particularly among Generation Z and Alpha cohorts. This comprehensive paper provides an extensive examination of the Reverse Flynn Effect through a multi-theoretical lens, integrating cognitive neuroscience, learning theory, ecological psychology, and emerging frameworks of technologically induced cognitive transformation. The analysis advances the argument that the observed decline represents not a genetic regression but an environmentally induced "cognitive restructuring"-a maladaptive adaptation to digital ecosystems that systematically outsource mental functions to external systems. The paper develops the Environmental Cognitive Constraint Model as an integrative framework for understanding how digital environments constrain the measurable expression of intelligence without necessarily reducing latent capacity. Three future scenarios are articulated-Continued Cognitive Erosion, Stabilization Without Recovery, and Successful Cognitive Adaptation-grounded in distinct technological trajectories and policy responses. The paper proposes a comprehensive solutions framework spanning individual behavioral protocols, educational reform, technological design principles, and public policy interventions. Key theoretical contributions include the refinement of the offloading/biloading distinction, the introduction of the False Cognitive Power Transfer (FCPT) concept, the articulation of the Cognitive Divergence Theory framework, and the development of the Memory Schema Depletion Hypothesis. The paper concludes that while the challenges are substantial, the neuroplasticity of the human brain and the potential for deliberate intervention provide grounds for measured optimism regarding the reversal of current trends.

title: (Re)learning to be Stupid, the Human Way
affiliations: Phenikaa University

detail.title: (Re)learning to be Stupid, the Human Way
detail.abstract: The AI era has blossomed, but it also marks the acceleration of the human brain-rot era: an age in which people can appear exceptionally intelligent with just a few lines of prompts, a subscription account, and enough electricity to power AI. The way to resist this tendency toward brain rot is to learn to be stupid like Kingfisher in Wild Wise Weird. In being stupid, Kingfisher appears more human than those who call themselves human while immersing themselves in the “perfect” world of AI. Only when people recognize their own stupidity do they have an opportunity to perceive their own absurdity—or, more precisely, the limitations of their epistemic systems.

title: Learning a Size-Weight Frontier for Synthetic-Augmented Inference
affiliations: and

detail.title: Learning a Size-Weight Frontier for Synthetic-Augmented Inference

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: The research is partially supported by the National Science Foundation grants DMS-2515679 and DMS-2544147.

detail.abstract: Synthetic data can improve statistical inference when real data are scarce, but naively treating synthetic samples as real data can introduce bias and lead to unreliable inference. We develop a general framework for synthetic-augmented inference across a population of related tasks. It characterizes synthetic augmentation by the number of synthetic observations and their weight. Central to our framework is a size-weight frontier that specifies, for each weight, the largest synthetic sample size for which all smaller sizes attain the target task-marginal coverage. We estimate this frontier from historical tasks, and establish a finite-sample coverage guarantee simultaneously for all size-weight configurations on or below the estimated frontier. In experiments using large language model responses to augment opinion survey data, our procedure achieves target coverage and substantially narrows confidence intervals.

title: Mothership-based truck-multi-drone cooperative delivery to moving targets: An event-driven multi-agent reinforcement learning approach
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Beijing Jiaotong University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Mothership-based truck-multi-drone cooperative delivery to moving targets: An event-driven multi-agent reinforcement learning approach
detail.abstract: In emergency logistics, road damage can make areas inaccessible to trucks, while rescuepersonnel, casualties in transit, and evacuees may remain mobile, causing their service locations to change over time. Conventional fixed-node delivery models are therefore not well suited to such settings. We study the moving-target truck-multi-drone mothership routing problem (MT-TMMRP), in which one truck serves as a mobile launch, recovery, and charging platform for two homogeneous drones operating in parallel. The problem jointly determines truck movement, drone task assignment, target interception, truck-drone meetings, and battery management to minimize total mission completion time. To represent these coupled operations, we formulate a continuous-space optimization model and an event-driven cooperative Markov game, and propose CAMS-MAPPO. The method uses environment feature encoding to capture relations among the truck, drones, and targets. It then employs the context-aware matching and scoring(CAMS) module to evaluate candidate support and service actions, while multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) learns a feedback policy reusable across instances. On small instances for which Gurobi proves optimality, CAMS-MAPPO achieves an average objective value gap of only 1.48% and reduces average online computation time by 97.64%. Across tests with different customer scales, the same policy parameters are reused without retraining and yield lower average completion times than the constructed ALNS baseline at every tested scale. Average online computation time remains below 0.7 s and is at least 99.88% lower than that of ALNS. Further analyses show diminishing returns from increases in battery capacity and the drone-to-truck speed ratio, whereas higher energy consumption extends mission completion time. Target speed, travel distance, and origin-destination distributions affect truck-drone routes and delivery performance by altering interception time windows and the operational range.

detail.title: Spatial Network and Driving Factors of Synergistic Reduction of Pollution and Carbon Emissions Governance in the Chengdu-Chongqing Economic Circle from a Green Energy Transition Perspective

keywords: Reduction of pollution and carbon emissions

detail.abstract: As the most densely populated urban agglomeration with the strongest industrial base in western China, the Chengdu-Chongqing Economic Circle (CCEC) hinges on synergistic reduction of pollution and carbon emissions governance (SRPCG) as a central issue for its regional green transition. From a green energy transition perspective, this study has developed a synergistic governance evaluation system encompassing government, enterprises, and the public. The study integrates the coupling coordination model, a modified gravity model, social network analysis, and an exponential random graph model to examine the evolution and driving factors of the spatial network for SRPCG in CCEC from 2018 to 2023. The results indicate: (1) The level of synergistic governance increases, with the coupling coordination degree rising from 0.543 to 0.757. However, most cities experience growth fluctuations between 2020 and 2022, indicating that system resilience requires further strengthening. (2) The spatial network evolves from a core-radiation pattern toward a dual-core-led, multi-cluster coordination pattern. Network density increases from 0.096 to 0.387 but remains relatively low, while subregional clusters begin to emerge. (3) The node of driving factors attributes weakens, giving way to structure-driven self-organization. By 2023, network structural factors like reciprocity, geographical distance, and economic disparity are the principal factors. (4) Clean-energy endowments have not yet become an effective source of collaborative ties, and differences in energy structure do not play a significant role in intercity network formation. This study provides empirical evidence and policy implications to help energy-rich urban agglomerations overcome the challenges of fragmented SRPCG.

title: Succession Over Accumulation: Feedforward as a Candidate Mechanism of Continuity

detail.title: Succession Over Accumulation: Feedforward as a Candidate Mechanism of Continuity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: This paper proposes that continuity is better understood as the elimination of the reconstruction event than as the minimisation of its cost-and that proactively transmitting a working model of prior reasoning (assumptions, constraints, rationale, and calibrated uncertainty, not merely conclusions) is a candidate mechanism for achieving this, distinct from and complementary to reactive, feedback-style reconstruction. Drawing on Wiener's distinction between feedforward and feedback control, and on the Conant-Ashby Good Regulator Theorem as theoretical motivation rather than formal proof, the paper argues that the unit of successful continuity is succession-the handoff of a working model of prior reasoning from one reasoning vehicle to the next-rather than accumulation of stored content. Organizational-learning and knowledge-continuity research has already established closely related distinctions between knowledge stocks and knowledge flows and between generic documentation and predecessor-to-successor knowledge transfer; this paper's narrower and more clearly novel contribution is applying that structure specifically to reasoning artifacts exchanged between AI and human reasoning vehicles, and proposing epistemic maturity marking as a necessary safeguard for any such artifact. The argument is offered as a conditional, falsifiable design hypothesis-not a theorem-illustrated but not established by an exploratory, uncontrolled cross-instance AI pilot.

title: Adaptive Feature Selection with Temporal Attention Network for Student Dropout Prediction
affiliations: United International University and United International University

detail.title: Adaptive Feature Selection with Temporal Attention Network for Student Dropout Prediction
detail.abstract: In higher education, student dropout is a major issue that impacts both institutional resultsand student well-being. Early prediction can lead to timely intervention, but current methodsoften struggle with temporal changes and with understanding relevant features. This paperintroduces AFS-TA (Adaptive Feature Selection with Temporal Attention Network), a novel deeplearning framework that merges adaptive feature selection, bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) with time-based attention mechanisms, and explainable artificial intelligence (AI) for dropout prediction. Our approach uses five feature ranking methods: Information Gain, Gain Ratio, Gini Index, Chi-squared, and Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) F-statistic. These methods help us pinpoint important predictors from 34 distinct features across academic, financial, and demographic domains. We have conducted extensive experiments on a real-world educational dataset with 4,424 students, organised into three outcome groups: 1,421 dropouts, 794 enrolled students, and 2,209 graduates. We have compared our results to six baseline models: Decision Tree (67.0%), Naïve Bayes (70.9%), Random Forest (76.7%), Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost) (74.2%), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) (75.9%), and Neural Network (71.4%). Our AFS-TA model has achieved impressive results with 91.30% accuracy and 95.5% area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC). Additionally, we have included SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based explainability for all models. This indicates that large language model (LLM)-derived engagement features and performance in courses are the most important predictors of dropout. The proposed framework covers the entire machine learning process, from data cleaning to model deployment, providing educational administrators with valuable insights through easy-to-understand visualisations.

title: Hybrid Feature Extraction Framework for Handwritten Signature Verification
affiliations: Adeleke University, Osun State University and Osun State University

detail.title: Hybrid Feature Extraction Framework for Handwritten Signature Verification
detail.abstract: Signature forgery detection is a critical aspect of authentication and security systems, particularly in financial and legal transactions. Existing studies predominantly rely on handcrafted algorithms that examine visual characteristics of signatures like size, shape, and stroke patterns. While useful, these approaches face limitations in feature quality and quantity, making them vulnerable to manipulation and ineffective against complex forgeries. This study proposes a principled hybrid framework that addresses the under-explored problem of combining complementary feature spaces; fine-grained local stroke patterns (local HOG), holistic structural context (global HOG), and discriminative deep representations (ResNet18); for robust expert forgery detection under resource constraints. MI-LASSO feature selection is specifically motivated by the sparsity requirements of high-dimensional biometric feature spaces.,The extracted features are concatenated into a unified feature vector and classified using a Random Forest classifier trained on an 80:20 stratified split, validated by 5-fold cross-validation and experimental results demonstrate an accuracy of 96.37% (mean CV: 96.21% ± 0.31%) on the SignBank dataset and 87.29% (mean CV: 87.09% ± 0.29%) on SigComp2011, with a 41% reduction in computation time at the optimal feature threshold of 8,000. An ablation study confirms that each feature modality contributes uniquely, with the hybrid combination outperforming the best single-modality baseline by 3.73% (SignBank) and 5.65% (SigComp2011). Inference time of 18.6 ms per sample enables throughput exceeding 50 verifications per second, making the framework well-suited for KYC and Fintech deployment. Future work will focus on optimizing and improving inference speed for deployment in cloud-based and mobile environments, enabling real-time verification.

title: Stable isotopes of precipitation in Angola (δ18O and δ2H): a first national baseline and the climatic controls of seasonal variability along the coast–inland gradient
