detail.title: Stable isotopes of precipitation in Angola (δ18O and δ2H): a first national baseline and the climatic controls of seasonal variability along the coast–inland gradient
detail.abstract: Angola, 1,246,700 km² spanning coastal desert to humid inland woodland, lies within the largest observational gap of the Global Network of Isotopes in Precipitation and had no published record of stable isotopes in precipitation. This work establishes the country's first isotopic baseline from 41 monthly samples collected in 2021–2022 at four stations in three provinces and analysed by cavity ring-down laser absorption spectroscopy. δ¹⁸O ranged from -8.05 ‰ to +0.11 ‰ and δ²H from -50.23 ‰ to +16.63 ‰, with deuterium excess (d) between 6.57 ‰ and 17.96 ‰. The national meteoric water line, δ²H = 7.69 δ¹⁸O + 11.79 (r² = 0.974; n = 41), has a slope statistically indistinguishable from 8 (95 % CI: 7.28–8.09), indicating condensation close to isotopic equilibrium across the sampled territory. Sub-cloud evaporation, commonly assumed to dominate in semi-arid climates, proved a strictly local signal confined to the peri-urban station of Zango 8000 (b = 6.76 ± 0.27; p = 0.001). The intercept of 11.79 ‰ exceeds the global value of 10 ‰, consistent with a recycled-moisture contribution. Deuterium excess increased inland at 0.71 ‰ per 100 km (r = 0.991; p = 0.009), reaching 13.85 ± 1.77 ‰ at N'Dalatando. Peak-rainfall months were significantly more depleted than the remaining months (-4.10 ‰ vs. -2.41 ‰; p = 0.003), confirming the amount effect as the dominant control, weakening inland. The results supply the local equation needed to interpret groundwater recharge and provenance in Angola and an observational anchor for regional isoscape calibration.

title: Rethinking Green Growth: Financial, Technological, and Consumption Indicators Across Developed and Developing Economies
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Rethinking Green Growth: Financial, Technological, and Consumption Indicators Across Developed and Developing Economies
detail.abstract: Understanding the factors associated with green-growth performance across different economic contexts is essential for advancing sustainable development. This study examines the financial, technological, and consumption-based dimensions associated with green growth across developed and developing economies. Using panel data for 91 countries over the period 2010–2020, green-growth performance is assessed using the composite Green Growth Index, while green investment, green innovation, Consumption Carbon Footprint (CCF), and key macroeconomic conditions are examined as potential correlates. The empirical analysis employs a two-way fixed-effects specification with country and year fixed effects, complemented by heterogeneity and robustness analyses.The findings reveal substantial heterogeneity across development levels. In developing economies, green investment, green innovation, and income levels are positively associated with green growth, while GDP growth exhibits a negative relationship. In developed economies, Consumption Carbon Footprint is negatively associated with green growth, while GDP growth similarly exhibits a negative relationship.These findings highlight the importance of considering financial and technological capacity alongside consumption-related environmental pressures within an integrated indicator-based perspective on green growth. The results suggest that the factors associated with green-growth performance differ across development contexts, with investment and innovation playing a more prominent role in developing economies and consumption-based environmental pressures emerging more strongly in developed economies. The study contributes cross-country evidence on the heterogeneous relationships between financial, technological, consumption-based, and macroeconomic indicators and green-growth performance and provides policy-relevant insights for developing context-sensitive strategies to support environmentally sustainable growth across diverse economic systems.

title: AI Talent Governance, Geopolitical Risk, and Brain Drain Risk in China's Artificial Intelligence Innovation System
affiliations: Peking University

detail.title: AI Talent Governance, Geopolitical Risk, and Brain Drain Risk in China's Artificial Intelligence Innovation System
detail.abstract: As AI emerges as a global technology with massive implications for society and the economy, external powers are beginning to explore how to govern AI talent around the world, and how their governance policies might in turn be affected by the governance of AI talent in other countries. With China rapidly rising as an AI powerhouse and other established tech powers such as the US and Europe now keeping a close eye on the sector, understanding the dynamics at play is increasingly critical. In this paper, the author explores the impact of the US’s geopolitical governance of AI talent in China—particularly as it relates to governance disruptions such as the restriction of AI technologies for export, the blacklisting of Chinese technology companies, and the restriction of collaborative research by American academics with their Chinese counterparts. Drawing on theories of global governance, foreign direct investment, human capital, and firm innovation, the author uses original empirical evidence from research institutions and technology companies engaged in AI to explore how governance disruptions related to the development and governance of AI research talent globally can affect China’s “brain drain” and domestic AI innovation. Combining novel data from the Thunear Global Chinese Researchers Database—a panel dataset of Chinese researchers at 340 research institutions in China and abroad—as well as a unique data set of 450 Made-in-China.com–certified companies that produce and integrate AI, the author finds that US export restrictions, the blacklisting of Chinese technology companies, and research restrictions on collaboration with Chinese academics significantly increase the likelihood that AI researchers from top Chinese universities and technology companies will choose to emigrate. Moreover, governance shocks affecting the sector of semiconductor and related global supply chains reduce AI-related innovation by Chinese research institutions. These negative effects on innovation are most pronounced for those universities and technology companies that engage in the most collaborative research with counterparts in foreign countries. New findings also provide governance counterfactual simulations that highlight possible paths to reduce brain drain losses by improving institutions’ ability to retain talent and facilitate greater mobility to international research destinations, particularly in developing countries. These results have important implications for redesigning the talent program run by China’s Ministry of Science and Technology and for bilateral agreements to send and host scientists to work on AI between countries. They also have lessons for broader governance of international research collaboration related to AI.

title: Hierarchical Energy Management for a P0/P2 Mild-Hybrid Electric Vehicle Using DDQN Supervisory Control and Adaptive ECMS
affiliations: Iran University of Science and Technology and Iran University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Hierarchical Energy Management for a P0/P2 Mild-Hybrid Electric Vehicle Using DDQN Supervisory Control and Adaptive ECMS
detail.abstract: This study proposes a hierarchical energy-management strategy for a 48-V dual-machine P0/P2 mild-hybrid electric vehicle, in which a double deep Q-network (DDQN) performs supervisory selection among EV, Series, and Parallel traction modes, while physically constrained mode-specific sub-controllers determine the continuous component commands. An adaptive ECMS controller was used to determine the torque-split in parallel drive. Regenerative braking is handled deterministically and excluded from exploratory control. The DDQN employs an 18-element observation vector incorporating vehicle demand, battery state, mode feasibility, supervisory memory, and internal A-ECMS states. Training uses episode-level randomization over NEDC, FTP, and HWFET, together with randomized initial SOC, vehicle mass, and auxiliary load. Three independent training seeds exhibit comparable convergence behavior, while removal of the SOC-away-drift term worsens the post-convergence mean reward from -19,035 to -31,941. A matched dynamic-programming benchmark is independently verified through Bellman reconstruction and discretization refinement. On the unseen driving cycles, the proposed agents achieved 95.45% and 92.8% of the DP-optimal fuel economy performance. Mean final SOC values are 59.4% and 59.69% from an initial 60%. Speed RMSE remains below 0.083 m/s, infeasible mode requests below 0.32%, and no hard SOC-limit violations occur. The results demonstrate that restricting reinforcement learning to supervisory mode selection addresses the dimensionality issue of direct component-level RL control and can provide near-optimal energy management while retaining feasible and interpretable lower-level control, with no prior knowledge of the driving information whatsoever.

title: A Surrogate-Assisted Multi-Objective Optimization Framework with Algorithm Comparison and Explainable Decision Support for Performance-Driven Building Design
affiliations: Tianjin Renai College, Pingdingshan University, Tianjin Renai College, Wuchang University of Technology, Tianjin Renai College, Tianjin University and Tianjin University

detail.title: A Surrogate-Assisted Multi-Objective Optimization Framework with Algorithm Comparison and Explainable Decision Support for Performance-Driven Building Design
detail.abstract: Performance-driven building design must simultaneously balance energy efficiency and thermal comfort-two inherently conflicting objectives. However, conventional simulation-based trial-and-error workflows are inefficient in exploring high-dimensional design spaces, and existing studies seldom integrate surrogate modeling, systematic algorithm comparison, and interpretable decision support within a unified framework. This study proposes a surrogate-assisted multi-objective optimization framework that chains Latin Hypercube Sampling, EnergyPlus-based dataset generation, a GA-BP neural network surrogate model, three representative multi-objective algorithms (NSGA-II, MOPSO, and MOGWO), performance benchmarking, and a three-level explainable decision-support strategy. The framework is instantiated on the DOE medium office reference building in Tianjin, China, optimizing eight design variables to minimize energy use intensity (EUI) and thermal discomfort hours (TDH). The GA-BP surrogate achieves high predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.9857 for EUI and 0.9979 for TDH), accelerating evaluation by a factor of 2.25 × 104. Systematic benchmarking over 30 independent runs reveals that MOPSO attains the highest and most stable hypervolume (178854 ± 6025), significantly outperforming NSGA-II and MOGWO (p < 0.001), while MOGWO is the fastest. Sobol’ sensitivity analysis identifies SHGC as the dominant driver of EUI and air tightness as the dominant driver of TDH. The knee-point design achieves a 4.5% reduction in EUI and a 29.4% reduction in TDH relative to the baseline. The framework is reproducible, architecture-agnostic, and provides actionable design guidance for performance-driven building design.

title: Collective Entrepreneurship as a Pathway to Financial Inclusion in Member-Owned Cooperatives: A Conceptual Framework and Research Propositions
affiliations: Nnamdi Azikiwe University

detail.title: Collective Entrepreneurship as a Pathway to Financial Inclusion in Member-Owned Cooperatives: A Conceptual Framework and Research Propositions
detail.abstract: Collective entrepreneurship and financial inclusion have developed as separate streams of scholarship, the former in cooperative and entrepreneurship studies and the latter in development finance. This paper develops an integrative conceptual framework explaining how collective entrepreneurship embedded in member-owned cooperatives generates demand-driven financial inclusion among members. Synthesising the entrepreneurship, collective action, cooperative organisation and financial inclusion literatures, the paper isolates four components of collective entrepreneurship (risk sharing, enterprise ownership, innovative training, and social capital) and maps them onto three recognised dimensions of financial inclusion: access, usage and quality. Collective entrepreneurship is theorised as an independent construct whose components influence inclusion outcomes through the cooperative's intermediating structure. Four core propositions are advanced: risk-sharing investment deepens savings usage; enterprise ownership strengthens loan usage; innovative training enhances loan quality and volume; and social capital reinforces savings usage and quality. Two further propositions specify how these relationships strengthen or weaken with cooperative size and membership tenure. The paper offers one of the first explicit conceptual bridges between collective entrepreneurship and financial inclusion, repositioning the cooperative as an entrepreneurial ecosystem in which shared risk, ownership, learning and relational capital jointly produce inclusion. The propositions provide a testable agenda for cooperative, entrepreneurship and development-finance researchers.

title: Health-aware bidirectional coordinated energy–thermal management for fuel cell hybrid commercial vehicles based on multi-agent TD3
affiliations: Wenzhou University, Wenzhou University, Wenzhou University, Wenzhou University, Wenzhou University, Wenzhou University, Wenzhou University and Wenzhou University

detail.title: Health-aware bidirectional coordinated energy–thermal management for fuel cell hybrid commercial vehicles based on multi-agent TD3
detail.abstract: To address the limited coordination among power allocation, thermal-state regulation, and auxiliary power consumption caused by the independent operation of the energy management system (EMS) and thermal management system (TMS) in fuel cell hybrid electric vehicles, this study proposes a health-aware bidirectional coordinated energy–thermal management strategy based on multi-agent twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (MATD3). A dual-agent EMS–TMS interaction framework is developed. The EMS agent determines the fuel cell power command by jointly considering vehicle power demand, battery state of charge (SOC), and thermal-management auxiliary loads, thereby coordinating the power split between the fuel cell and battery. Meanwhile, the TMS agent optimizes the cooling-pump and radiator-fan actions according to variations in fuel cell power and thermal states, with the objectives of stabilizing the thermal conditions and reducing auxiliary energy consumption. Simulation studies are conducted under the China Heavy-duty Commercial Vehicle Test Cycle (CHTC), and the proposed strategy is benchmarked against deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) and proportional–integral–derivative (PID) control strategies. The results show that MATD3 significantly improves the dynamic power characteristics of the fuel cell. Compared with DDPG and PID, the standard deviation of fuel cell power is reduced by 82.72% and 65.25%, respectively, while the total fuel cell power variation is reduced by 63.91% and 58.14%, thereby mitigating the degradation risk associated with frequent power fluctuations. MATD3 also achieves superior SOC regulation, with a final SOC of 0.595. The cumulative hydrogen consumption is 228 g, representing reductions of 8.1% and 22.7% compared with DDPG and PID, respectively. The total operating cost is 11 RMB, corresponding to reductions of 21.42% and 31.25%. In addition, MATD3 achieves better performance in fuel cell and battery degradation mitigation, fuel cell temperature regulation, and thermal-management auxiliary power optimization. Overall, the proposed strategy enables coordinated improvements in operating economy, power-source durability, and thermal stability.

title: Reconfiguring Sustainable Business Models through Stakeholder Engagement: A Strategizing Perspective
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and EDC Paris Business School

detail.title: Reconfiguring Sustainable Business Models through Stakeholder Engagement: A Strategizing Perspective
detail.abstract: Digital small ventures (DSVs) operate in digitally enabled and highly interdependent environments in which sustainable business model innovation (SBMI) increasingly depends on actors and resources beyond organizational boundaries. Yet existing SBMI research insufficiently explains how heterogeneous stakeholders become participants in the strategic work through which sustainable value is created, delivered, and captured. This study examines how stakeholder engagement contributes to the strategizing of SBMI in such ventures. Drawing on an abductive qualitative study of 21 French DSVs, complemented by secondary materials, we conceptualize Open Sustainable Business Model Innovation (OSBMI) as a stakeholder-enabled strategizing process through which external actors participate in designing, orchestrating, and appropriating economic, social, and environmental value. Our findings identify three interconnected activities through which OSBMI unfolds: collaborative sustainable value design, distributed sustainable value orchestration, and plural sustainable value appropriation. We further identify five project-based stakeholder engagement strategizing configurations—Primary Economic, Social and Inclusive, Environmental and Efficiency, Social and Territorial Impact, and Ecosystem Balance—which differ in stakeholder composition, engagement modes, and sustainability orientations. The findings reveal a recursive pattern whereby stakeholder configurations shape how sustainable value is designed, orchestrated, and appropriated, while experimentation and learning reshape stakeholder dependencies and the configurations mobilized in subsequent projects. The study advances SBMI and Strategy-as-Practice research by showing how stakeholder engagement becomes constitutive of strategizing, thereby extending the locus of sustainable business model strategizing beyond organizational boundaries.

title: Lambda R{\'e}nyi entropic value-at-risk
affiliations: University of Science and Technology of China (USTC)

detail.title: Lambda R{\'e}nyi entropic value-at-risk
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Lambda extension of the R\'{e}nyi entropic value-at-risk ($\Lambda$-EVaR), a novel family of risk measures that unifies the flexible confidence level structure of the $\Lambda$-framework with the higher-moment sensitivity of EVaR. We define $\Lambda$-EVaR, establish its foundational properties including monotonicity, cash subadditivity, and quasi-convexity, and provide a complete axiomatic characterization showing that convexity, concavity in mixtures and cash additivity hold only when $\Lambda$ is constant. A dual representation and an extended Rockafellar-Uryasev-type formula are derived, enabling efficient computation. We further analyze the worst-case behavior of $\Lambda$-EVaR under Wasserstein and mean-variance uncertainty, obtaining closed-form expressions that reveal its robustness properties. The proposed measure bridges the gap between adaptive risk tolerance and moment-sensitive risk assessment, offering a versatile tool for modern risk management.

title: Strategic Calibration: How Organizations Configure Proportionate Responses to Environmental Change

detail.title: Strategic Calibration: How Organizations Configure Proportionate Responses to Environmental Change
detail.abstract: Organizations confronting environmental change must determine not only whether to respond, but how to configure their response. Existing research explains how organizations interpret change, determine the magnitude and timing of strategic adjustment, preserve flexibility under uncertainty, coordinate interdependent activities, and learn from feedback. Yet these dimensions have largely been theorized separately, although organizations must configure them jointly. This article develops a theory of strategic calibration, defined as the organizational process through which the magnitude, timing, speed, sequencing, and reversibility of strategic response are configured relative to interpreted environmental significance, persistence, uncertainty, and scope. The framework conceptualizes strategic response as a multidimensional configuration and distinguishes under-adjustment, over-adjustment, and cross-dimensional miscalibration. It further identifies interpretive distortion, inherited commitments, and organizational coordination constraints as mechanisms generating miscalibration, while showing how action and feedback enable recalibration. The theory shifts strategic adaptation from a question of how much organizations change toward how they configure change under uncertainty.

title: Structural Analysis and Prioritization of Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Risks: A Hybrid FTISM–MICMAC Framework with MoSCoW and Rank Sum Weighting
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST) - NUST Business School, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Structural Analysis and Prioritization of Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Risks: A Hybrid FTISM–MICMAC Framework with MoSCoW and Rank Sum Weighting
detail.abstract: The pharmaceutical industry has a strong connection with human health and wellness and is thus considered a very important part of the nation’s economy and public welfare. Being an integral part of the supply chain of drugs, pharmaceutical firms face several risks that could hinder their ability to deliver medicine effectively. The disruption could have effects on the quality, amount, and timely availability of the products to the intended recipients. Even though there could be the continuation of the operation of the supply chain of pharmaceuticals without taking note of these risks, the success, sustainability, and resilience of the supply chain would be greatly affected. Thus, it is very important to determine some of the major risks to improve the performance of the supply chain. Based on some of the challenges in this regard, this research is aimed at determining those risks that cause disruption in the pharmaceutical supply chain. Initially, potential risks were established through a literature review and further prioritized on the basis of expert opinion. This research involved the application of Fuzzy Total Interpretive Structural Modelling and MICMAC (Cross-Impact Matrix Multiplication Applied to Classification) for the structural analysis of the risks. Further, MoSCoW and rank sum techniques have been used for the prioritization of the risks identified. The study reveals that, ”unpredictable trade barriers” is the most significant risk, while ”limited suppliers” follows next among 20 risks. Additionally, this study is also a contribution to the existing body of literature as it has discovered four more risks.

title: The Impact of Employee Ownership on the Strategic Orientation of Foreign Direct Investment: Governance Matters
affiliations: University of Montana, Durham University and Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

detail.title: The Impact of Employee Ownership on the Strategic Orientation of Foreign Direct Investment: Governance Matters
detail.abstract: FDI motives are typically explained by external location advantages and institutional differences. International business research has paid less attention to how internal governance structures influence FDI. We examine whether employee ownership, operationalized as S-corp ESOPs, conditions the motives of outward FDI. Drawing on stakeholder-oriented governance theory and the capability-based perspective, we argue that employee ownership heightens sensitivity to strategies that impose concentrated domestic labor costs while favoring investments aligned with long-term capability upgrading. We test these arguments using 37,968 US outward greenfield FDI projects (2003–2023) matched to tax-based records identifying S-corp ESOP firms. Multinomial logit models show that ESOP firms are significantly less likely to undertake efficiency-seeking projects and significantly more likely to pursue strategic asset-seeking FDI than non-ESOP firms. We did not find any systematic difference in market-seeking behavior between ESOP and non-ESOP firms. These findings position employee ownership as a governance-based micro-foundation of FDI motives.

title: Corporate Governance Mechanisms and Environmental Management Accounting Implementation: The Moderating Role of Corporate Social Responsibility Performance
affiliations: Padjadjaran University, Padjadjaran University, Padjadjaran University and Padjadjaran University

detail.title: Corporate Governance Mechanisms and Environmental Management Accounting Implementation: The Moderating Role of Corporate Social Responsibility Performance
detail.abstract: This study tests how institutional ownership, managerial ownership, and audit committee effectiveness shape environmental management accounting implementation, and whether corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance moderates these relationships. Institutional ownership is measured as the percentage of shares held by institutional investors relative to total outstanding shares. This study operationalizes audit committee effectiveness through three indicators commonly used in governance research: the number of annual committee meetings, the proportion of independent members, and members' financial and environmental expertise. CSR performance uses the PROPER rating from Indonesia's Ministry of Environment, scored on a five-point scale (Gold = 5, Green = 4, Blue = 3, Red = 2, Black = 1). Environmental management accounting implementation uses a GRI-based disclosure index: each firm scores 1 for a disclosed item and 0 for an omitted one, summed across all items. Using Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) on five years of firm data, the results show that institutional ownership and audit committee effectiveness predict environmental management accounting implementation; managerial ownership does not. CSR performance moderates the audit committee relationship but not the ownership relationships. Firms that pair stronger governance with stronger CSR performance embed environmental accounting more deeply into their sustainability strategy the two reinforce each other rather than working in isolation.

title: Effectiveness of food safety management systems and their role in food loss reduction: Evidence from Egyptian food manufacturing firms
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Effectiveness of food safety management systems and their role in food loss reduction: Evidence from Egyptian food manufacturing firms
detail.abstract: Purpose This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of food safety management systems (FSMSs) and examine whether FSMS effectiveness contributes to food loss reduction in food manufacturing firms. Design/methodology/approach Primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to 35 firms. A composite Food Safety Effectiveness Index (FSEI) was developed based on 12 indicators covering operational practices, organizational efficiency and supply chain management. The analysis employed both Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) and Ordered Logit models, with the latter used as the main estimation approach due to the ordinal nature of the dependent variables. Findings The results indicate that food safety system effectiveness is generally moderate. GFSI-recognized certifications significantly enhance system effectiveness, while firm age shows a negative association. The findings also reveal a statistically significant inverse relationship between food safety system effectiveness and food loss levels. In addition, product diversification and firm age contribute to reducing food loss. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance of improving the implementation of food safety management systems to enhance operational efficiency and reduce food loss in food manufacturing firms. Originality/value This study provides firm-level empirical evidence linking food safety system effectiveness with food loss, offering an integrated approach to assessing how management practices influence performance in the food manufacturing sector.

title: Networks and innovation life cycle: Forty years of inter-city knowledge flows in mRNA vaccine development
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Italian National Research Council (CNR-ISSIRFA) and National Research Council (CNR)

detail.title: Networks and innovation life cycle: Forty years of inter-city knowledge flows in mRNA vaccine development
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the evolving structure of the inter-city knowledge flow network underlying the full life cycle of mRNA vaccine innovation, from early basic research in the mid-1980s to the commercialisation of COVID-19 vaccines in 2020. Drawing on 24,442 patents and 4,412 inventors across 46 countries and 1,281 cities, we construct a directed temporal network and analyse its structural evolution relying on the innovation life cycle model. Our results show that concentration is not an enduring structural property but an emergent outcome: the initial phase of the innovation process is characterised by dispersed, non-hierarchical flows and weakening hub dominance, while the second phase consolidates around a stable hierarchy of dominant cities. These findings suggest that innovation policy should account for the phase-dependence of network structure, avoiding premature concentration of resources in the early stages of technological development.

title: Carrier responses to off-hour delivery policy scenarios: The role of receiver demand and perceived non-carrier constraints
affiliations: National University of Colombia, University of the North and Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (RPI)

detail.title: Carrier responses to off-hour delivery policy scenarios: The role of receiver demand and perceived non-carrier constraints
detail.abstract: This paper examines how freight carriers respond to off-hour delivery (OHD) policy scenarios, focusing on the relationship between carrier perceptions of non-carrier actors and OHD selection. Using stated-choice panel data from freight carriers in Barranquilla, Colombia, we estimate a hybrid panel choice model combining policy attributes with latent perceptions of the carrier–receiver relationship and the urban operating environment. The model incorporates power over the receiver, trust in the receiver, perceived freight infrastructure constraints, and perceived night-time insecurity. The results show that carriers are more likely to select OHD when a higher proportion of receivers request night-time deliveries, and when OHD offers savings in terms of travel time and fuel costs. Greater perceived power over receivers is positively associated with OHD selection, while perceived night-time insecurity strongly reduces it. Infrastructure constraints are indirectly relevant through their negative association with trust in receivers. These findings provide evidence from the carrier's perspective for designing voluntary OHD programmes that combine receiver engagement, operational incentives, and safer night-time delivery conditions.

title: Who Supports Transit? Individual and Geographic Predictors of Transit Policy Attitudes in Canada
affiliations: Western University

detail.title: Who Supports Transit? Individual and Geographic Predictors of Transit Policy Attitudes in Canada
detail.abstract: Public transit investment is a debated question in Canadian municipal governance, yet we know little about what shapes public support for it across urban contexts. I examine transit and urban mobility policy attitudes among a nationally representative sample of 6,949 Canadians drawn from the 2025 Canadian Municipal Barometer, linked to a novel Transit Quality Index measured at the census tract level across all 41 Canadian census metropolitan areas. I address three questions: how transit attitudes vary across Canadian cities, what individual-level factors predict them, and whether neighbourhood-level transit quality shapes investment support independently of individual characteristics. I find that transit attitudes are primarily structured by individual-level factors, particularly political ideology and commute mode, while city membership explains only a small share of total variance. Neighbourhood-level transit quality, measured through a composite index of transit supply, accessibility, and time competitiveness, is not significantly associated with transit investment support, hinting at a quality paradox. This null result holds across two outcome variables and both ordinary least squares and multilevel estimation. These findings suggest that public support for transit investment in Canada is embedded in the ideological and behavioural cleavages that structure Canadian politics more broadly, and is largely insensitive to the quality of existing transit systems.

title: Optimal Consumption under Smooth Ambiguity
affiliations: Ulm University - Institute of Insurance Science and Ulm University

detail.title: Optimal Consumption under Smooth Ambiguity
detail.abstract: We study how individuals choose contingent consumption plans when the probabilities of future states are ambiguous and utility depends on the realized state. In both static one-period and intertemporal smooth-ambiguity settings, we show that ambiguity aversion shifts the decision-maker's subjective prior and alters the discount factor. We provide explicit sufficient conditions that characterize these shifts, clarifying how to identify a "worse" prior and how intertemporal consumption trade-offs amplify ambiguity's impact. Applying our framework to insurance economics, we illustrate how ambiguity aversion offers a compelling explanation for the "underinsurance puzzle'' and the "annuity puzzle''---two longstanding challenges to standard expected-utility models.

title: Pre-Expiration Liquidity and Price Reactions to IPO Lockup Expirations
affiliations: and

detail.title: Pre-Expiration Liquidity and Price Reactions to IPO Lockup Expirations
detail.abstract: This study examines whether pre-expiration stock liquidity is associated with cross-sectional variation in price reactions to a potential increase in the supply of tradable shares, using IPO lockup expirations as pre-scheduled events. We construct a hand-collected dataset of lockup contracts from IPO disclosure documents for 522 IPO firms listed on the Mothers market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange between 2012 and 2021. Because lockup expiration dates are determined at the time of the IPO, this setting mitigates concerns that event timing is chosen in response to contemporaneous market conditions. We find a negative median cumulative abnormal return (CAR) around lockup expirations, and the magnitude of the reaction varies systematically with pre-expiration liquidity. Firms with higher pre-expiration turnover experience higher CAR, and this association remains significant in the joint specification. Higher Amihud illiquidity is associated with lower CAR in separate specifications, whereas wider bid-ask spreads show a marginally significant negative association; neither association remains statistically significant in the joint specification. The liquidity–CAR association is concentrated in the post-expiration window and is not statistically significant in the pre-expiration window, consistent with variation in post-expiration price reactions rather than pre-existing return trends. Overall, pre-expiration liquidity is associated with cross-sectional variation in post-expiration price reactions, with the most robust evidence coming from turnover.

title: Classifying Indoor Thermal Environments to Examine Simpson-type Aggregation Effects on Adaptive Comfort Models for Chilean Housing
affiliations: Universidad San Sebastian, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Chile, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Concepción, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Classifying Indoor Thermal Environments to Examine Simpson-type Aggregation Effects on Adaptive Comfort Models for Chilean Housing
detail.abstract: Adaptive thermal comfort models are used to evaluate naturally ventilated buildings. However, they generally treat comfort data samples as homogeneous populations, masking differences in thermal satisfaction between environments. This study analyzes whether classifying homes by their measured indoor temperature profiles before developing comfort models allows identifying differentiated adaptive responses and better represents them than a single aggregate model. Environmental conditions were monitored for 15 months in 116 naturally ventilated homes across 14 Chilean cities. The application of unsupervised clustering techniques such as k-means allowed identifying two indoor thermal profiles. Subsequently, linear and segmented adaptive models were developed for each cluster and for the total sample. The segmented models identified points of change in average outdoor operating temperature between 11.99 and 12.62 °C. Below these points, the slopes differed in both magnitude and direction: -0.220 for cluster A, 0.129 for cluster B, and 0.054 for the aggregated sample. As a result, Simpson's paradox occurred through effect modification and an aggregation-induced distortion of the association. The empirical 80% acceptability intervals showed an asymmetric distribution and extended further towards cold conditions, with displacements ranging from -5.73 to +3.73 °C across the different models. These findings show that the previous classification of indoor thermal environments reveals adaptive heterogeneity that may be hidden in aggregated models. The proposed approach can contribute to the development of more context-sensitive comfort assessments and climate resilience indicators. However, a higher declared tolerance should not be interpreted as direct evidence of healthy conditions or unlimited adaptive capacity.

title: Heated Surface Modification, Channel Orientation and Mass Flow in Rectangular Minichannel Flow Boiling: Comparative Analysis and Multi-Model Machine Learning Validation
affiliations: Kielce University of Technology

detail.title: Heated Surface Modification, Channel Orientation and Mass Flow in Rectangular Minichannel Flow Boiling: Comparative Analysis and Multi-Model Machine Learning Validation
detail.abstract: This study combines working-fluid-resolved descriptive contrasts of heated-surface condition, spatial orientation and nominal mass-flow level with provenance-safe multi-model machine-learning validation for flow boiling in rectangular minichannels. The integrated archive comprises 64,385,791 reconstructed point-level records from 449 experimental source files spanning six dielectric fluids, smooth and developed surfaces, multiple orientations and several flow levels. The physical analysis is organised around three matched-contrast questions. The matched-cell analysis indicates a strongly fluid-dependent surface response, orientation ratios that are frequently close to parity under comparable conditions, and a more directionally consistent positive response to increasing nominal mass flow in the broader subcooled subsets. These contrasts are treated as descriptive rather than causal because the archive is heterogeneous and not factorially balanced. The predictive analysis compares Histogram Gradient Boosting (HGB), XGBoost, CatBoost and an architecturally independent multilayer perceptron (MLP) under increasingly stringent source-file and fluid-domain validation. On the retained common source-file split, MLP produced the higher Nusselt number R2 (0.912 versus 0.892), whereas HGB produced the higher heat transfer coefficient R2 (0.865 versus 0.837). Across five repeated source-file group splits, HGB had the higher mean R2 for both targets, while leave-one-fluid-out validation was substantially more demanding. Permutation importance was dominated by net heat flux, while the surface identifier and orientation angle had low global incremental importance; these importances are predictive rather than causal. The combined results distinguish conditional experimental contrasts, within-domain new-experiment generalisation and transfer to an unseen working-fluid domain.

title: Hierarchical Physics-Constrained Information Fusion for Pattern Recognition in Sparse-View 3D Tomography
affiliations: Southwest University of Science and Technology, Southwest University of Science and Technology and Southwest University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Hierarchical Physics-Constrained Information Fusion for Pattern Recognition in Sparse-View 3D Tomography
detail.abstract: Reconstructing three-dimensional volumetric patterns from sparse, near-field two-dimensional projections remains a fundamental challenge in computational imaging and multi-modal perception, where depth ambiguity and occlusion-induced phantom artefacts routinely undermine reconstruction fidelity. To address this ill-posed inverse problem, we propose a Hierarchical Physics-Constrained Information Fusion architecture that progressively collapses spatial uncertainty through sequential physical, statistical, and geometric constraints. Rather than relying on late-stage heuristic overlay, the proposed architecture operates across three inference tiers. In Tier 1, the Physical Constraint Prior, a multi-channel convolutional neural network surrogate acts as a physics-informed encoder, mapping discrete hardware parameters to spatial tensors and circumventing computationally prohibitive Monte Carlo simulations while tightly bounding the physical solution space. In Tier 2, the Statistical Uncertainty Estimation, a dynamic-response generalized expectation-maximization algorithm synthesizes distance-correct response matrices, adaptively resolving near-field depth mismatch and restoring focal sharpness with provable monotonic log-likelihood ascent. In Tier 3, the Geometric Uncertainty Collapse, a distributed Logarithmic Opinion Pool consensus protocol cross-validates two-dimensional probability heatmaps against three-dimensional exteroceptive structural constraints, enforcing Boolean intersection across orthogonal views to deterministically eliminate phantom artefacts. Extensive physical experiments in heavily occluded environments demonstrate that the proposed paradigm reduces the mean three-dimensional localization error from 0.86 ± 0.29 metres to 0.05 ± 0.01 metres. This architecture establishes a generalizable probabilistic framework for sparse-view tomographic pattern recognition, bridging physics-enhanced learning and multi-agent geometric consensus.

title: Layered Sequential Injection: A Novel Numerical Framework for Three-Layer Stratified Ammonia Dual-Fuel Combustion
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Layered Sequential Injection: A Novel Numerical Framework for Three-Layer Stratified Ammonia Dual-Fuel Combustion
detail.abstract: Ammonia is a promising zero-carbon fuel for compression-ignition engines, but its poor ignition characteristics and slow combustion kinetics necessitate the use of a supporting fuel to enhance combustion. Among the dual fuel strategies proposed for this purpose, the three-layer stratified injection concept, in which a supporting fuel sandwiches the ammonia within a single injection pulse, has shown considerable promise in suppressing N2O emissions and improving combustion efficiency. Simulating this layered sequential injection process numerically is challenging, as the distinct fuel layers are delivered in a single injection pulse from a single nozzle. This study proposes the Layered Sequential Injection (LSI) numerical framework to address this challenge, using spatially coincident but temporally phased virtual injectors to replicate the layered delivery of ammonia and n-hexadecane within a single injection pulse. Two strategies are proposed: a 4-injector LSI strategy, in which each virtual injector delivers a homogeneous mixture of ammonia and n-hexadecane, and a 6-injector LSI strategy, which additionally hypothesizes that the boundaries of the injection pulse are dominated by pure n-hexadecane. Both strategies are evaluated against published experimental data for a constant volume combustion chamber under non-reacting and reacting conditions. Under non-reacting conditions, the 6-injector LSI reproduced the experimental spray penetration and morphology considerably better than the 4-injector LSI. Under reacting conditions, the 6-injector LSI successfully captured the evolution of chamber pressure and heat release rate. of the ammonia stratified injection process, validating the proposed framework against experimental measurements. The LSI framework provides a general, validated numerical tool for simulating and optimizing layered injection strategies.

title: Coalitional Stability in a Class of Social Interactions Games
affiliations: Boston College - Department of Economics, University of Toulouse I - GREMAQ-IDEI and Southern Methodist University (SMU) - Department of Economics

detail.title: Coalitional Stability in a Class of Social Interactions Games
detail.abstract: In this paper, we define additive dyadic social interactions games (ADG), in which each player cares not only about the selected action, but also about interactions with other players, especially those who choose the same action. This class of games includes alliance formation games, network games, and discrete choice problems with network externalities. While it is known that games in the ADG class admit a pure strategy Nash equilibrium that is a maximizer of the game's potential, the potential approach does not always apply if all coalitional deviations are allowed. In this paper, we systematically identify both restrictions on possible coalitional deviations to preserve the potential function and types of equilibria that ensures their existence for various subclasses of ADG or its subclasses, extending the approach taken by Le Breton et al. (2021). An additional avenue of our results is the examination of games with outside option which expand the set of alternatives. Although this modification complicates the analysis significantly, positive results are obtained with different class of restrictions.

title: Creditor Rights and the Reallocation of Institutional Ownership: Does Group Affiliation Matter?
affiliations: and Indian Institute of Management Raipur

detail.title: Creditor Rights and the Reallocation of Institutional Ownership: Does Group Affiliation Matter?
detail.abstract: This study examines how institutional investors reallocate equity holdings following a strengthening of creditor rights and whether firms’ organizational structure shapes this response. Exploiting the introduction of India’s Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) as a quasi-natural experiment, we employ a difference-in-differences design using a propensity-score-matched sample of standalone and business-group-affiliated firms over 2010–2019. We find that institutional ownership increases more in business-group-affiliated firms than in standalone firms following the IBC. Consistent with a risk-buffering mechanism, group-affiliated firms experience a smaller increase in leverage-induced risk after the reform. The differential increase in institutional ownership is concentrated among firms with higher pre-IBC leverage and systematic risk and is more pronounced for firms affiliated with larger and more diversified business groups, which have greater capacity to absorb financial shocks. The response is driven primarily by mutual funds and foreign institutional investors, while financial institutions exhibit no statistically significant differential response. Overall, our findings suggest that institutional investors respond to cross-sectional differences in the financial downside exposure associated with stronger creditor rights by reallocating capital toward firms with greater capacity to withstand financial distress.

title: Attention-Guided Dual Masking and Dynamic Text Refinement for Text-to-Image Person Re-Identification
affiliations: Yonsei University, Yonsei University, Yonsei University and Yonsei University

detail.title: Attention-Guided Dual Masking and Dynamic Text Refinement for Text-to-Image Person Re-Identification
detail.abstract: Recent approaches for text-to-image (T2I) person re-identification (reID) typically rely on pretraining with large-scale unlabeled person images. Specifically, given an unlabeled person image, these methods employ multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to generate corresponding textual descriptions, which are used to train a vision-language model, e.g., CLIP. The pretrained models are then transferred to target reID datasets. In this paper, we identify two critical limitations of existing pretraining schemes. First, the text encoder of CLIP tends to focus on a limited set of tokens, many of which are not necessarily informative for discriminating person IDs. This underrepresents fine-grained attributes carrying ID-discriminative cues. Second, the textual descriptions generated by MLLMs are inherently noisy. In some cases, a description generated for one image may be more semantically aligned with another image. To address these limitations, we propose a novel pretraining framework for T2I reID. Specifically, we introduce attention-guided dual masking (AGDM), which adaptively masks words in textual descriptions that show high attention scores but do not provide ID-discriminative cues. We also propose dynamic text refinement (DTR), which dynamically refines noisy textual descriptions generated by MLLMs using cross-modal similarities between image-description pairs. Extensive experiments on standard person reID benchmarks, including CUHK-PEDES, ICFG-PEDES, and RSTPReid, demonstrate that our method achieves a new state of the art, validating the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

title: Efficient three-dimensional indoor pollutant field prediction using a dynamic point-sampled residual DeepONet
affiliations: Tsinghua University, Nanjing Tech University, Tsinghua University, Tsinghua University and Tsinghua University - The Institute of Public Safety Research

detail.title: Efficient three-dimensional indoor pollutant field prediction using a dynamic point-sampled residual DeepONet
detail.abstract: High-resolution three-dimensional pollutant-field prediction is computationally demanding because dense spatial supervision substantially increases the cost of surrogate-model training. This study develops a dynamically point-sampled neural operator for efficient prediction of steady indoor pollutant concentration fields. The concentration field is represented as a continuous function of operating conditions and spatial coordinates, while only a dynamically resampled subset of CFD points is used for supervision during each training update. The framework was evaluated on 2,000 steady-state CFD scenarios in a fixed mechanically ventilated enclosure, each containing approximately 300,000 spatial points. Sampling-density analysis identified a stable range of 256–8,192 points per case. The 1,024-point setting achieved the lowest weighted mean absolute percentage error (WMAPE) of 18.14%, while using 256 points reduced the supervised spatial points per update by approximately 99.9% with limited loss of full-field accuracy. Further compression below 128 points primarily degraded high-concentration prediction. The proposed ResDeepONet achieved a WMAPE of 18.66%, compared with 23.33% for a conventional coordinate-based multilayer perceptron. Cross-resolution evaluation from 19,200 to 1,012,500 query points showed that WMAPE remained within 0.34 percentage points of the native-grid result, including predictions on independently refined CFD grids. A complete 300,000-point field was reconstructed in approximately 0.20 s, with inference cost scaling with the number of requested coordinates. These results demonstrate that dynamic point-sampled operator learning enables accurate, resolution-flexible, and computationally efficient prediction of high-resolution three-dimensional pollutant fields.

title: Academic Leadership in the Boardroom and Corporate Green Breakthrough Innovations: The Moderating Role of Internal R&D Intensity
affiliations: Peking University

detail.title: Academic Leadership in the Boardroom and Corporate Green Breakthrough Innovations: The Moderating Role of Internal R&D Intensity
detail.abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine if academic leaders can assist businesses in developing scientifically sound new ideas and whether in-house research and development departments can supplement or replace external scientific consultants. This research examines resource dependency theory through the lens of resource supply using panel data collected from 991 publicly listed, innovative U.S. enterprises. To determine if there is a correlation between having academic directors and developing ground-breaking ideas grounded in science, the empirical research examines the publication histories of various firms. To test the robustness of our findings, we use instrumental variable analysis in conjunction with natural experiments driven by the untimely death of prominent academics. The findings demonstrate a robust correlation between the involvement of academic directors and advancements in scientific knowledge. Companies with a longer publishing history have a greater positive correlation, demonstrating that in-house R&D knowledge and outside academic knowledge are complementary rather than mutually exclusive. Additionally, we demonstrate that the findings are robust when using instrumental variable analysis in conjunction with natural studies centred on the unexpected deaths of eminent academics. These findings reinforce the correctness of the main points. The role of strategic leadership in facilitating science-based innovation and increasing the innovation potential of enterprises via the use of external academic information is further illuminated by these findings. Businesses and policymakers should work towards better connections between academic research and corporate R&D if they want to encourage innovative breakthroughs.

title: A Convex Standardization-Based Squashing Function for Capsule Networks
affiliations: Yildiz Technical University, Yildiz Technical University and Albany State University

detail.title: A Convex Standardization-Based Squashing Function for Capsule Networks
detail.abstract: Deep learning architectures often struggle to efficiently model hierarchical part-whole relationships in visual data. Capsule Networks (CapsNets) offer a structured alternative to Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for addressing this challenge; however, their performance is constrained by the standard squashing function, which intro-duces information bottlenecks through sub-optimal activation compression. This paper presents a convex standardization-based squashing function that augments the standard quadratic normalization term with a layer-wise standardization step using mean and variance statistics, scaled by a fixed coefficient to improve optimization stability. By stabilizing activation distributions across capsule layers, the proposed method maintains gradient flow while preserving capsule orientation information. The formulation enhances information flow by preserving 15.3% more inter-layer mutual information compared to the baseline squashing function and reducing gradient saturation. Experimental results on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and Lung Cancer datasets using stratified 5-fold cross-validation demonstrate statistically significant improvements over the baseline CapsNet. When comparing the two squashing functions based on information-theoretic analyses such as higher entropy retention, gradient signal-to-noise ratio, and effective bottleneck dimensionality the results confirm that applying information-theoretic principles to activation design enhances representational capacity, improves classification performance, and accelerates convergence. With the newly proposed squash function, the objective is to achieve a more effective and robust learning process in CapsNet applications while simultaneously ensuring more accurate data classification. Ablation studies demonstrate the proposed function's compatibility with dynamic routing and EM-based routing mechanisms. The framework is generalizable and can be integrated into normalization layers and attention modules for broader deep learning applications.

title: LRNet: A Dual-Path Attention Network with Residual Connections for Image Classification
affiliations: Beijing Institute of Technology, Hebei University of Engineering, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing Institute of Technology and Beijing Institute of Technology

detail.title: LRNet: A Dual-Path Attention Network with Residual Connections for Image Classification
detail.abstract: Despite the dominance of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in computer vision, conventional single-path architectures inherently struggle to capture both fine-grained details and global context. This trade-off between spatial resolution and receptive field size is particularly acute in complex scenes requiring multi-scale feature integration. To address this, we propose LRNet, a novel dual-path architecture with residual-enhanced attention mechanisms, where parallel pathways process high-resolution local features and down-sampled global context, dynamically fused through channel-spatial-cross attention modules. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100 demonstrate state-of-the-art performance with 93.8% accuracy, with ablation studies confirming the individual contributions of dual-path design, attention fusion, and residual connections performing 18% faster convergence. This work provides a principled framework for adaptive feature aggregation, with potential extensions to hierarchical visual recognition tasks beyond classification.

title: When Not to Adapt: Conservative Slack-Aware Online Test-Time Adaptation for Real-Time Video Perception
affiliations: University of Missouri, University of Missouri and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: When Not to Adapt: Conservative Slack-Aware Online Test-Time Adaptation for Real-Time Video Perception
detail.abstract: Online test-time adaptation (TTA) is typically motivated by robustness under deployment-time shift, yet in real-time video systems adaptation is also a control decision: adapting at the wrong moment can increase latency and deadline misses without delivering reliable quality gains. We study online TTA for streaming object detection from this deployment-oriented perspective. Starting from a slack-aware controller family driven by predictive uncertainty, temporal drift, and measured latency slack, we compare inferenceonly, always-on, periodic, confidence-gated, and slack-aware policies on selected BDD50 videos, a large-scale BDD1000 brightness benchmark, and labeled real-video pseudo-streams with compression and blur stress tests, and show that the strongest deployment operating point is a simplified conservative no-drift variant. The extended experiments support three findings. First, always-on and confidence-only adaptation are operationally unsafe: on the labeled real-video benchmark they raise p95 latency to 32.87 ms and 32.37 ms, respectively, with deadline-miss ratios of 4.70% and 2.58%. Second, richer controller branches do not automatically improve the final operating point; removing the strongest escalation action has negligible effect, and removing drift improves or matches labeled F1 while reducing timing risk. Third, the simplified conservative slack-aware policy, SafeSlack, matches inferenceonly on labeled quality, reaching F1@0.5 of 0.4386 and AP50 of 0.1899, while avoiding the timing failures of aggressive adaptation. These results suggest that real-time TTA should be evaluated as a joint perception-and-systems

title: Does Common Institutional Ownership Distort Human Capital Allocation? Evidence from Labor Investment Efficiency
affiliations: Ningbo University of Finance and Economics and National Central University

detail.title: Does Common Institutional Ownership Distort Human Capital Allocation? Evidence from Labor Investment Efficiency
detail.abstract: This study examines whether common institutional ownership (CIO) is associated with labor investment efficiency using a large panel of U.S. public firms from 1993 to 2022. We find that higher CIO is associated with lower labor investment efficiency, with additional evidence suggesting that this association may be concentrated in delayed workforce downsizing. This result contrasts with the efficiency-enhancing role documented for conventional and foreign institutional ownership, suggesting that common ownership may constitute a boundary condition to the monitoring benefits of institutional investors. The negative association is stronger in highly competitive industries and among firms with lower financial reporting quality. Results from propensity score matching and a merger-based difference-in-differences analysis are broadly consistent with the baseline findings. Overall, common ownership may weaken firm-level responsiveness in workforce adjustment.

title: A dual-branch deep learning framework for site-to-pixel upscaling of in situ albedo measurements: Accounting for spatial heterogeneity and scale effects
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Southwest Jiaotong University, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), Zhejiang Normal University, Southwest Jiaotong University, Southwest Jiaotong University and Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS)

detail.title: A dual-branch deep learning framework for site-to-pixel upscaling of in situ albedo measurements: Accounting for spatial heterogeneity and scale effects
detail.abstract: Pixel-scale reference ”truth” serves as a critical link between in situ measurements and satellite observations. However, owing to surface heterogeneity, the upscaling of single-site observations to the satellite pixel scale has long been constrained by poorly understood mechanisms of heterogeneity effects, inadequate characterization of nonlinear responses, and insufficient utilization of spatial information. Existing methods, particularly machine learning approaches, generally adopt a direct point-to-pixel mapping strategy that implicitly assumes mutual independence among subpixels within a coarse pixel. This assumption conflicts with the spatial autocorrelation inherent in a spatially continuous land surface, thereby introducing systematic biases into upscaling results over heterogeneous land surfaces. To address this challenge, we propose a site-to-pixel upscaling method that integrates environmental attribute modeling with spatial context learning. The core of this method is a parallel dual-branch architecture comprising a multilayer deep neural network and a convolutional neural network. The former establishes a nonlinear mapping between environmental attributes and the target variable, whereas the latter extracts multiscale spatial heterogeneity patterns within the coarse pixel. The features from the two branches are then adaptively fused through a gating mechanism, followed by spatial aggregation using a point spread function. Evaluation across 416 globally distributed sites encompassing 15 land cover types shows that the model achieves R² values of 0.802–0.997 and RMSE values of 0.007–0.032. At sites jointly affected by spatial heterogeneity and topographic complexity, the median RMSE is more than 30% lower than that of the best-performing benchmark model. Ablation experiments show that the combined mechanism of per-subpixel modeling and residual learning is the primary source of model accuracy improvement, reducing RMSE by more than 60%. The complete dual-branch model accurately reproduces the spatial texture and spatial variability patterns within coarse pixels. Using MCD43A3 product validation as an example, the upscaled reference reduces validation RMSE by 10.2%–22.4%; at highly heterogeneous sites, Bias is reduced by 85.7%. This study demonstrates that the proposed method effectively enhances the ability of in situ observations to represent pixel-scale conditions over heterogeneous surfaces, providing a reliable and cost-effective solution for generating high-quality pixel-scale reference ”truth” and a fundamental basis for remote sensing product validation and the construction of pixel-scale training samples.

title: Monetary Policy Transmission, Shadow Banking, and Corporate Investment in China: A Sign-Restricted Bayesian SVAR and Local-Projections Analysis
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Monetary Policy Transmission, Shadow Banking, and Corporate Investment in China: A Sign-Restricted Bayesian SVAR and Local-Projections Analysis
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the joint transmission of Chinese monetary policy and shadow-banking dynamics to corporate investment using a monthly macro-financial dataset spanning 2005M1–2025M12 (252 observations). We employ two complementary identification strategies: a sign-restricted Bayesian structural vector autoregression (SVAR) that allows for uncertainty around the identification of monetary and shadow-banking shocks, and the Jordà (2005) local-projections (LP) estimator that avoids the compounding of specification error at longer horizons. Both approaches deliver a coherent picture: a 25-basis-point contractionary shock to the PBoC 7-day repo rate reduces corporate investment growth by approximately 0.35 percentage points at peak (12 months post-shock), while a positive shock to wealth-management-product (WMP) outstanding raises investment by 0.45 percentage points at the 6-month horizon. Forecast-error variance decompositions attribute approximately 38 % of the 24-month-ahead variance of investment to monetary and shadow-banking shocks jointly. Bank-level heterogeneity is substantial: smaller and more shadow-banking-dependent lenders transmit contractionary shocks with materially larger elasticities. The paper contributes new time-series evidence on the macro-financial architecture of Chinese monetary policy.

title: House Prices, Household Leverage, and Financial-Stability Risk in Chinese Cities: A Nonlinear Panel-Threshold Analysis
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: House Prices, Household Leverage, and Financial-Stability Risk in Chinese Cities: A Nonlinear Panel-Threshold Analysis
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the nonlinear relationship between household leverage, house prices, and financial-stability risk across 70 major Chinese cities over 2010–2025 (N × T = 1,120 observations). We deploy three complementary nonlinear panel estimators: the Hansen (1999) fixed-effects panel-threshold model, the González–Teräsvirta–van Dijk (2005) panel smooth-transition regression (PSTR), and the Canay (2011) fixed-effects panel-quantile estimator. All three approaches deliver a coherent picture. First, the response of the non-performing-loan (NPL) ratio to the household debt-to-income (DTI) ratio is strongly nonlinear: below a DTI threshold of approximately 0.55 the elasticity is 0.60, whereas above the threshold it rises to approximately 4.10, a nearly seven-fold amplification. Second, the PSTR estimator delivers a smooth transition with a location parameter c = 0.548 and slope parameter γ = 6.5, closely aligned with the Hansen breakpoint. Third, quantile regressions show that the marginal effect of leverage on NPL at the ninth conditional decile (τ = 0.90) is approximately nine times the effect at the first decile (τ = 0.10). Fourth, the amplification is more pronounced in Tier-1 and Tier-2 cities, where the average house-price-to-income ratio is substantially higher. The historical decomposition attributes approximately 46 % of the post-2019 rise in aggregate NPL growth to accumulated household-leverage effects, and highlights the importance of a differentiated, region-specific macro-prudential framework.

title: Damage-adaptive conformal prediction for reliable remaining useful life prognostics of lithium-ion batteries under missing and faulty capacity telemetry
affiliations: Northwestern Polytechnical University, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Northwestern Polytechnical University and Northwestern Polytechnical University

detail.title: Damage-adaptive conformal prediction for reliable remaining useful life prognostics of lithium-ion batteries under missing and faulty capacity telemetry
detail.abstract: Data-driven models now predict the remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries with good accuracy in the laboratory. Field telemetry is less kind. Capacity readings drop out, sensors drift, and whole cycles go unrecorded. Under such corruption a model’s point error grows visibly, while its prediction intervals fail silently: they keep the nominal confidence label but lose the actual coverage. We present a prognostic framework that keeps both accuracy and stated confidence when the capacity channel is damaged. A bidirectional LSTM receives causally imputed state-of-health values together with explicit missingness indicators, and is trained on damage-augmented data. A split conformal wrapper then scales the interval width with the corruption rate observed in each input window. The adaptivity parameter is tuned on a dedicated calibration subset, which preserves the finite-sample coverage guarantee. We test on 31 cells from four public datasets over ten repeated cell-level splits. At severe corruption the point error falls from 0.240 to 0.138 in fraction-of-life units. The adaptive intervals hold the 90% target at every damage level, where fixed-width intervals fall to 0.843 and a clean-calibrated pipeline collapses to 0.540. Deployment needs only the observed fraction of missing data.

title: A Quantitative Analysis of the Equity Return Consequences of Sovereign Default Risk
affiliations: University of Seoul

detail.title: A Quantitative Analysis of the Equity Return Consequences of Sovereign Default Risk
detail.abstract: This paper evaluates the extent to which standard quantitative sovereign default models exhibit equity return responses around default risk spikes comparable to the data. It finds that they largely do not. Hébert and Schreger (2017) employ a high-frequency event study around legal rulings and report a 10% increase in default risk causes a 6% decline in firms’ market value. A workhorse sovereign default model augmented with capital accumulation delivers only a 0.2% equity value drop. Three features account for the disconnect: the absence of private capital outflows and trade surpluses during default, the model’s counterfactual prediction of rising dividends, and the nominal depreciation embedded in the dollar-denominated index used in the data.

title: Broadband Infrastructure and Industrial Productivity: How Institutional Quality Shapes Digital Returns in China
affiliations: Jilin University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Jilin University and Old Dominion University

detail.title: Broadband Infrastructure and Industrial Productivity: How Institutional Quality Shapes Digital Returns in China
detail.abstract: Does digital infrastructure automatically generate productivity dividends, or do institutional conditions shape its returns? This paper examines broadband penetration and manufacturing labor productivity using panel data from 30 Chinese provinces over 2012–2023. Fixed-effects estimation yields a significant positive effect (β = 0.89, p < 0.05). A Hansen panel threshold test identifies a significant threshold at marketization index 7.31 (p < 0.001), but a Wald test reveals the cross-regime coefficient difference is statistically insignificant (p = 0.60). A continuous interaction model fits better (ΔAIC = 14.76), with a positive interaction term (β = 0.28, p < 0.01), indicating that marketization functions as a gradual amplifier rather than a binary switch. Exploiting the staggered rollout of the ”Broadband China” demonstration city policy as a quasi-natural experiment, event study confirms parallel pre-trends (joint F-test: p = 0.907). While the average treatment effect is statistically insignificant, heterogeneous DID reveals that the policy’s effect on industrial output is strongly moderated by marketization (interaction β = 751.56, p < 0.01). Mechanism analysis identifies technological innovation as the primary transmission channel (β = 165.02, p < 0.001). The evidence implies that institutional reform should accompany digital infrastructure investment to maximize industrial productivity gains—though in provinces with weaker institutions, broadband investment requires careful governance to avoid counterproductive outcomes.

title: Assessing the level of agroecological transitions in family farming in Madagascar’s Central Highlands
affiliations: University of Antananarivo, University of Antananarivo, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Assessing the level of agroecological transitions in family farming in Madagascar’s Central Highlands
detail.abstract: AbstractContext: Given the current challenges facing agriculture, agroecology is emerging as a promising strategy for improving the sustainability and resilience of agricultural systems, particularly for family farms. In the Central Highlands of Madagascar, agroecological practices are promoted through various projects. However, quantifying them remains difficult and complex.Objective: This study aimed to assess the level of agroecological integration among 486 family farms in the Vakinankaratra and Itasy regions of Madagascar.Methods: Based on the agroecology assessment guide developed by the Groupe de Travail sur les Transitions Agroécologiques (GTAE), we adapted and validated an agroecological integration score tailored to the context of the Central Highlands of Madagascar. The score is constructed from 19 components grouped into six main dimensions: crop and livestock diversity, ecological synergies, resource economy and recycling, self-reliance based on the utilization of local resources, soil protection, and contribution to territorial dynamics. These dimensions provide a comprehensive understanding of farms’ commitment to the agroecological transition.Results and conclusions: The results show an average score of 30.72, indicating that the farms studied are generally at a “moderately agroecological” level. However, this average masks significant heterogeneity among farms, which exhibit varying levels of progress in the agroecological transition. Certain practices are already well established, notably crop diversification and the recycling of organic matter. In contrast, other areas, such as soil protection, animal vaccination, or the optimization of ecological interactions, remain underdeveloped. Overall, agroecology is already present in the Central Highlands, particularly through so-called traditional practices. Nevertheless, additional efforts are needed to strengthen this transition. It therefore appears essential to support producers through training programs, exchanges of experiences, and tailored technical assistance.Significance: This study provides a practical way to better understand how family farms in Madagascar are progressing toward agroecology. By revealing the practices that are already well established and those that still require support, it offers useful insights for researchers, policymakers, and development practitioners to design more effective actions and help farmers strengthen their transition toward more sustainable farming systems

title: International Redesign and Validation of the Management Accounting Theoretical Framework: A Mixed-Methods Approach
affiliations: , University of Tehran and Khatam University

detail.title: International Redesign and Validation of the Management Accounting Theoretical Framework: A Mixed-Methods Approach
detail.abstract: This study intends to redesign and validate, on an international scale, a model for developing a management accounting conceptual framework using a mixed-methods approach. The research adopts an applied-developmental purpose and utilizes an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 16 management accounting experts, including both academics and practitioners. After achieving theoretical saturation, data were analyzed using grounded theory through open, axial, and selective coding. In the quantitative phase, the identified items were transformed into a questionnaire and administered across six international contexts, resulting in 640 valid responses. Data analysis used confirmatory factor analysis, reliability and validity indices, Wilcoxon, Kruskal-Wallis, and Friedman tests, as well as Kendall’s W and Borda count logic. Qualitative findings indicate that the management accounting conceptual framework is based on causal, contextual, and intervening conditions, as well as strategies and consequences, all organized around the central phenomenon of framework redesign. Quantitative results confirm the model's optimal fit, satisfactory construct reliability and validity, and relative consensus across multiple international contexts. The findings suggest that the conceptual framework provides relevant, reliable information and supports decision-making, contingency fit, sustainability, professional judgment, and measurability. Through integrating qualitative theorizing with quantitative validation, this study provides a coherent model to advance research, education, professional standardization, and the maturity assessment of management accounting systems in contemporary organizations.

title: Deep Learning-Based Intelligent Intrusion Detection and Risk Alert Model for Cybersecurity
