detail.title: Deep Learning-Based Intelligent Intrusion Detection and Risk Alert Model for Cybersecurity
detail.abstract: To address the limitation in unknown threat identification rates caused by spatiotemporal feature coupling in high-dimensional heterogeneous network communication, this paper proposes an intelligent intrusion detection and dynamic early warning model that integrates graph manifold topological convolution and multi-scale temporal attention. This architecture employs a parallel dual-track module, capturing node topological features through spectral domain operations using Chebyshev polynomials, extracting the evolutionary semantics of temporal sequences using a Transformer component with causal masks, and finally, joint feature analysis by a cross-domain gating unit. Experimental results show that when processing network traffic datasets with imbalanced distributions, the model achieves a combined accuracy of 98.67% and a cross-domain recall of 96.15%, demonstrating a performance improvement over the baseline temporal architecture. Risk assessment tests based on Mahalanobis distance show that the model's truncation response latency for concealed attack sequences is controlled within 56.8 milliseconds, providing theoretical and methodological support for intelligent defense under high concurrency conditions.

title: Neural Network-Based Multidimensional Attack Feature Mining and Identification for Cybersecurity
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Sungkyunkwan University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Neural Network-Based Multidimensional Attack Feature Mining and Identification for Cybersecurity
detail.abstract: Dynamic evolution modeling and correlated identification of multidimensional attack features constitute a core scientific problem in cybersecurity situational awareness. To address the bottlenecks of fragmented alerts and difficult attack-chain reconstruction faced by conventional defense systems under multi-stage compound attacks, this study proposes a neural-network-based method for multidimensional attack feature mining and identification. The method constructs a three-stage progressive analytical framework: a multidimensional feature mining network extracts heterogeneous features from three orthogonal dimensions—traffic, vulnerability, and attack behavior; a multi-scale spatiotemporal evolution and fusion module explicitly models cross-dimensional spatiotemporal co-evolution dynamics through multi-branch spatiotemporal receptive-field units and dimension-wise channel convolutions; and a multi-head self-attention model reconstructs attack chains and classifies attack intent from the evolved representations. On a semi-physical synthetic dataset containing 12 million flow records, the proposed method achieves 93.2% attack-chain reconstruction completeness and an F1 score of 96.8%, surpassing the strongest baseline by 14.8 and 5.1 percentage points, respectively. Mean detection latency is reduced to 210 s, and recognition accuracy for previously unseen attack variants reaches 89.6%. These results demonstrate that introducing multiscale spatiotemporal modeling into cybersecurity situational awareness effectively resolves the problem of dynamic evolution modeling and correlated identification of multidimensional attack features, providing new methodological support for precise threat perception in complex attack scenarios.

title: Retirement, Consumption, and Liquidity: Evidence from Norway
affiliations: University of Oslo, Statistics Norway and Institute for Social Research, Norway

detail.title: Retirement, Consumption, and Liquidity: Evidence from Norway
detail.abstract: We study household consumption and savings around retirement using comprehensive administrative data from Norway and a major pension reform implemented in 2011. The reform altered access to early pension claiming and labor supply incentives for private-sector workers, allowing us to distinguish between liquidity effects and changes in incentives and lifetime resources. We first show that household income and consumption move closely together over the life cycle but that consumption does not exhibit a discrete drop at retirement, despite a decline in disposable income. Exploiting the reform in a difference-indifferences framework, we find that expanded access to liquidity leads to only modest and delayed increases in consumption, with no evidence of anticipation effects prior to eligibility. By contrast, for workers whose labor supply incentives were strongly affected by the reform, we observe clear increases in income, consumption, and savings from the pension-eligible age onward. These results suggest that liquidity primarily shapes the timing of consumption responses, while changes in incentives and realized income paths determine their magnitude.

The research employs a dialogic model of interpretation, integrating rationalist frameworks and structural analyses of political, cultural, and socioeconomic conditions. The paper examines the historical trajectory of Sudan, the rise of Islamic fundamentalism, and the impact of the National Islamic Front (NIF), later the National Congress Party, on state policy and society. The analysis includes a review of Sudan's constitutional and legal transformations, policies influencing economic development, and the ideological schism driving civil conflict, culminating in events such as the Darfur crisis. Conclusions address the discrepancy between theoretical ideals and practical realities, shedding light on the challenges of implementing religious ideology within a heterogeneous society.

title: Overcoming Industrial Data Deficits via Target Domain Pivoting: A Hybrid Normal Behavior Modeling and LSTM Framework for Wind Turbine Stator Prognostics

detail.title: Overcoming Industrial Data Deficits via Target Domain Pivoting: A Hybrid Normal Behavior Modeling and LSTM Framework for Wind Turbine Stator Prognostics
detail.abstract: Industrial wind turbine structural health monitoring (SHM) requires robust anomaly detection to prevent catastrophic sub-system failures. This paper presents a complete end-to-end prognostic framework that integrates irregular, event-based status logs with continuous 10-minute SCADA data grids. Facing severe data omissions in traditional gearbox thermal channels discovered within the public Zenodo Penmanshiel dataset, an automated discovery routine isolated the generator stator domain as an uncompromised tracking target. A virtual sensor baseline is built using an XGBoost Normal Behavior Model (NBM) trained exclusively on healthy operational intervals to filter out stochastic wind variations, achieving an out-of-sample Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 2.7950°C. The resulting thermodynamic residuals are converted into a rolling 24-hour standard deviance to formulate a continuous Stator Health Index tracking path from 100% down to 0%. A regularized Deep LSTM network was trained chronologically over unshuffled 3D tensors to map path-dependent wear trajectories. Validated on the Penmanshiel 11 asset, the architecture tracks out-of-sample component degradation with high fidelity, achieving a validated structural R² tracking score of 0.5533 and a low validation MAE of 6.1763%.

detail.abstract: The Red Sea corridor carries approximately 12% of global trade, yet it has evolved into a complex geopolitical arena where great power interests, regional ambitions, and logistics competition converge. This paper assesses the potential shift of regional trade from the centralized Dubai hub (Jebel Ali Port) toward a decentralized or direct model centered on Port Sudan. Using a mixedmethod analysis of trade data, infrastructure assessments, sanctions frameworks, and geopolitical realignments (2023-2026), the study quantifies potential losses for Jebel Ali and identifies the reexport ecosystem and gold trade as the most vulnerable segments. Three scenarios are developed: continued "creative chaos," the Saudi-led Red Sea integration, and an Eastern rogue route under Russian-Chinese barter systems. The paper concludes that while Jebel Ali will not collapse operationally, the erosion of its value-added services and gold-based financial intermediation poses a long-term strategic threat. Policy recommendations focus on diversification, railway rehabilitation, and sanctions compliance.

title: Expert-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Uncertainty-Aware Planning and Real-Time Operation of Building-Integrated Energy System

detail.title: Expert-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Uncertainty-Aware Planning and Real-Time Operation of Building-Integrated Energy System

keywords: Twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient

detail.abstract: Uncertainty in renewable generation, weather, and multi-energy demand complicates capacity planning and real-time operation of building-integrated energy systems. This study develops a planning-to-operation framework combining correlated scenario generation, two-stage stochastic mixed-integer linear programming, and expert-guided reinforcement learning. Correlated uncertainty scenarios are generated and reduced for stochastic capacity planning. The resulting capacities define an operational model that produces 300 expert trajectories for behavior-cloning pretraining, critic warm-up, and decaying expert regularization of twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient. A deterministic feasibility layer converts policy commands into executable schedules. Across 200 independent out-of-sample days, the stochastic capacity design reduces cooling-shortage probability from 61.0% to 27.0%, annual cooling energy not supplied by 66.6%, and annual cost excluding shortage penalties by 1.06% relative to the annual-mean-day design. Across the same operating days and five random seeds, BC-TD3 attains a mean cost of 2,148.16 USD day⁻¹, 1.41% above the perfect-forecast MILP benchmark and 25.31% below conventional TD3. It also produces schedules approximately 60 times faster than MILP. Ablation results show that behavior-cloning pretraining establishes most of the economic performance, whereas continued expert regularization prevents degradation during TD3 updates. The shared feasibility layer produces executable schedules for all evaluated policies, while BC-TD3 reduces request–execution MAE by 94.3% relative to conventional TD3. These results demonstrate that uncertainty-aware capacity planning improves out-of-sample supply reliability, while expert-guided reinforcement learning supports near-optimal and computationally efficient operation within the evaluated 24-h setting.​

detail.abstract: Sudan's post-independence history represents one of the most protracted and complex cases of state failure in the modern era, characterized by recurrent civil wars, systemic marginalization of peripheries, and an unresolved constitutional crisis concerning the relationship between religion and the state. This paper argues that the binary framing of Sudan's crisis as a choice between an Islamic state and a secular state fundamentally misrepresents the structural, economic, and historical dimensions of the conflict. Through demographic analysis, historical examination of constitutional developments, socioeconomic assessment of center-periphery disparities, and critical evaluation of peace processes, the paper demonstrates that Sudan's tragedy stems not from the unresolved religion-state question alone, but from the confluence of exploitative governance patterns inherited from pre-colonial and colonial eras, inequitable resource distribution, the instrumentalization of religious identity by political elites, and the failure of peace processes to address root causes. Drawing on the Addis Ababa Agreement (1972), the Comprehensive Peace Agreement (2005), the Juba Peace Agreement (2020), and contemporary proposals for national consensus, the paper proposes a framework for moving beyond the sacred-secular binary toward a constitutional settlement grounded in citizenship rights, institutional reform, and equitable federalism. The paper concludes that sustainable peace in Sudan requires not the victory of either Islamist or secularist visions, but a fundamental reimagining of the Sudanese state as a civic, federal, and inclusive polity that guarantees equal citizenship for all its diverse peoples while respecting their religious and cultural identities.

detail.abstract: This working paper examines a recurring rule-of-law problem in civil enforcement: whether judicial protection remains effective when compulsory enforcement can produce serious or practically irreversible consequences before a competent court has had a meaningful opportunity to examine a substantive challenge to the creditor's claim. The paper is based on a documented Latvian enforcement sequence involving an enforceable judicial instrument, active enforcement measures in August 2026, a separate civil action filed on 26 August 2026 contesting the legal basis, amount, assignment chain and calculation of the claim, and a refusal on 28 August 2026 to suspend enforcement. The central thesis is deliberately narrow. A valid enforcement instrument is ordinarily enforceable, and the filing of a separate civil action does not automatically suspend execution. Equally, a sworn bailiff is not the forum for finally adjudicating the underlying civil-law dispute. The rule-of-law question arises at the point between those propositions: national procedural law must make available a competent judicial mechanism capable of reviewing contested enforcement and, where the statutory conditions are satisfied, preserving the status quo before later judicial review loses practical value. The analysis addresses Section 632 of the Latvian Civil Procedure Law, Article 92 of the Constitution of Latvia, Articles 6 and 13 of the European Convention on Human Rights, Article 1 of Protocol No. 1, and-insofar as the dispute falls within the scope of European Union law-Article 47 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights and the EU principle of effectiveness.

title: Non-Tariff Restrictions in International Trade: Economic Effects and Regulatory Practices

detail.title: Non-Tariff Restrictions in International Trade: Economic Effects and Regulatory Practices
detail.abstract: This article examines non-tariff measures (NTMs) as an increasingly important instrument of international trade regulation. It explores the concept, principal classifications, and dual nature of NTMs, which may pursue legitimate public-policy objectives-such as the protection of human, animal, and plant health, consumer safety, environmental protection, and national security-while also functioning as indirect forms of protectionism. The study assesses the economic effects of non-tariff restrictions on trade flows, market access, transaction costs, product prices, competition, and consumer welfare. Particular attention is paid to technical barriers to trade, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, quantitative restrictions, licensing procedures, export controls, subsidies, and trade-related investment measures. The article demonstrates that the growing use of NTMs contributes to the fragmentation of global markets and creates disproportionate compliance costs for exporters from developing economies. The paper also considers the international legal framework for non-tariff regulation, including the WTO Agreements on Technical Barriers to Trade and on the Application of Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures. Finally, it compares regulatory practices in the United States and Russia, taking into account the Eurasian Economic Union framework, sanctions-related restrictions, import-substitution policies, and the growing role of technical and administrative requirements in trade policy. The article concludes that an effective trade-policy framework should balance the protection of national interests with transparency, proportionality, and the preservation of open international trade.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how strongly firm-level zombie status in Japan comoves with aggregate economic conditions. Thus, dominant aggregate factors alone explain relatively little, while broader macroeconomic information provides additional explanatory power.

detail.abstract:
For me Sudan is not a distant country through diplomatic statements, policy papers, or television reports. I write as a Sudanese citizen, as a survivor of captivity and torture, and as a witness to aspects of the United Arab Emirates’ involvement in Sudan.

My position is therefore not abstract. It comes from experience, from what I have seen, from what I have endured and from watching my country and its people suffer while much of the world either remains silent or insists on explaining Sudan to the Sudanese.

I believe in Sudan’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and right to preserve its national institutions. But defending Sudan does not mean pretending that the Sudanese government has performed well. It has not. It is weak, disorganised and often appears to operate without a clear national plan, without an effective political vision and without a convincing strategy for leading the country out of war.

That weakness has added to the suffering of the Sudanese people.

However, the failure of the government does not give Britain, the UAE or any other foreign power the right to choose alternative representatives for Sudan, design our future behind closed doors or trFor me eat our sovereignty as an obstacle to their preferred political arrangement.

Sudan needs help. It needs enormous international support. But there is a difference between helping a wounded country stand again and taking advantage of its weakness to decide who should govern it. That distinction lies at the heart of the controversy surrounding the Wilton Park meeting.

detail.abstract: In February 2010, Chile was struck by the Maule earthquake, which measured 8.8 on the moment magnitude scale and dealt a severe blow to the local manufacturing sector. This paper treats the Maule earthquake as an exogenous shock to Chile's manufacturing sector to examine how the sector recovered in the aftermath of the earthquake, whether this recovery spilled over into the labor market, and whether the recovery had heterogeneous effects on unskilled and skilled workers. I address this question using a difference-in-differences design across industries and regions. The results show that, among the variables examined (output, employment, labor productivity, the labor share of output, proxy measures of profits, and investment), only investment responded to capital reconstruction, while no significant changes were observed in the other indicators. However, since the severely affected central urban regions already had higher investment levels than other areas prior to the disaster, I treat this evidence as a lead rather than a definitive conclusion. The paper primarily demonstrates that reconstruction restored the capital stock but did not alter the scale of production or the allocation of resources.

title: What Lies Behind Investment Banking, Shadow Banking, and High-Frequency Trading? A Risky, Dangerous, Secretive, or Reputable Business?

detail.title: What Lies Behind Investment Banking, Shadow Banking, and High-Frequency Trading? A Risky, Dangerous, Secretive, or Reputable Business?

detail.abstract:
Investment banking, shadow banking, and high-frequency trading are among those manifestations of modern finance that evoke fascination and mistrust in equal measure. Drawing on the academic literature and on current data from international institutions (Financial Stability Board, ESMA, SEC, LSEG), this paper examines what these lines of business actually are, how they function, who conducts them, and whose interests they serve.
The analysis shows that all of the activities examined constitute legal, economically well-founded, and in large part regulated businesses whose questionable reputation stems chiefly from opacity, conflicts of interest, and isolated excesses. Investment banking is a highly concentrated business of a few large banks, with worldwide fee income of $60.5 billion in the first half of 2025 alone. Shadow banking, as recorded by the Financial Stability Board, comprises assets of $256.8 trillion and thus already 51 per cent of the global financial system. In high-frequency trading, roughly 55 per cent of US and up to 43 per cent of European equity trading volume is attributable to strategies whose reaction times are measured in millionths of a second; the costs associated with latency arbitrage amount to roughly five billion dollars per year worldwide (Aquilina, Budish, and O'Neill, 2022).
For investors, a differentiated assessment follows: none of the businesses examined is disreputable per se, and none is free of risk. Those who understand how they work, who the participants are, and where the profits originate can weigh opportunities and dangers realistically — and may, in selected cases, participate in these markets themselves, whether through listed trading firms or through regulated credit funds.

title: How Much Green Is Enough? Green Investing between Regulation, Returns, and Impact

detail.abstract:
This paper examines green investing: its origins, the European regulatory regime, the categories and product classes, and the question of what green security selection means for returns, costs, and real-world environmental impact. The analysis is written from the perspective of a financial analyst and relies exclusively on publicly available regulatory documents, index and product data covering the last ten years, and the empirical research literature.
Three results stand out. First, in broad markets the return differences between conventional indices and their green variants are small over ten years — the MSCI World SRI returned 13.2 per cent per annum against 13.3 per cent for its parent index — whereas strict screens in narrow markets produce large gaps (United Kingdom: 4.8 versus 9.0 per cent per annum). Second, for bonds of identical credit quality, maturity, and currency, the yield concession on green securities (the greenium) currently amounts to zero to four basis points for government bonds and is close to zero for corporate bonds. Third, green index products now cost about the same as conventional ones (differences of a few basis points); among actively managed funds, ESG funds are on average even cheaper than funds without an ESG focus.
As regards real-world impact: buying a share in the secondary market provides the company with no capital, and according to the empirical evidence exclusion decisions shift the cost of capital of the affected firms by mere fractions of a basis point. What demonstrably works are binding laws — such as the European emissions trading system — together with engagement and financing through the primary market. Green investing is therefore first and foremost an expression of preferences and a filter within risk management, but not a reliable driver of returns. Rules for investors are derived from these results.

detail.abstract: Net neutrality got flip-flopped for a decade because it was built on agency reclassification. The lack of laws surrounding its existence led to it being struck down for lack of statutory authority. AI regulation is heading in the same direction. The new executive orders are legally weaker than net neutrality and the next administration can just undo them. Only Congress passing a statute creates durable AI law. The fix is a two-tiered federal framework, modeled on Sarbanes-Oxley: ordinary-risk models operate under self-certification and liability, while catastrophic-risk models face FDA-style pre-market approval, plus liability for misuse similar to how gun manufacturers are treated. Congress passed SOX almost unanimously after Enron and WorldCom. The point is to legislate the AI framework proactively, before we have another collapse.

detail.abstract:
This paper deals with the largest transfer of wealth in postwar history: in Germany, up to around EUR 400 billion changes hands every year through inheritances and gifts, in Austria around EUR 15 billion with a rising trend. Written from the perspective of a financial analyst, the paper asks what testators and heirs must pay attention to so that the transfer produces the best possible return-before, during, and after the handover. It describes the heir generations Y, Z, and Alpha, the legal position in Germany and Austria (as of August 2026), and the role of wealth management through 2035.
The results in brief: For testators, the planned, early, and step-by-step handover is the single most effective measure — in Germany because of the personal allowances that renew every ten years, in Austria because transfers are tax-free but subject to reporting duties and to forced-share rules; retained-use rights and contractual reclaim clauses protect the giver. For heirs, a simple structure applies: build a reserve, repay expensive debt, invest cash wealth in broadly diversified, globally oriented equity funds with a long-term investment horizon, direct current income predominantly into monthly equity savings plans, and examine inherited real estate soberly — use it yourself if it fits your life, otherwise sell it in order to downsize and stay mobile.
By 2035, wealth management will be judged by its ability to accompany transitions rather than sell products: more than two thirds of heirs do not stay with their parents' adviser after the handover. Whoever wants to keep the heir generation must involve it early, work digitally and personally at the same time, and serve smaller fortunes with suitable, opportunity-rich investment solutions. A separate chapter is devoted to women, who in the great handover usually inherit twice — as widows and as daughters — and whose longer lives, more interrupted working biographies, and disciplined investment behaviour wealth management can answer in a targeted way. Concrete advice for both sides of the transfer is derived from the analysis.

detail.abstract: Food supply networks consist of complex, intertwined relationships among firms that depend on each other for flows of goods and services. Even in "commodity"markets, transactions between firms involve contracts and long-term relationships in which prices and other terms are set through a negotiation process, so bargaining power is key. Importantly, the stability of these relationships determines the resilience of the entire network through disruptions that may interrupt the normal flow of goods and services. We estimate the importance of bargaining power and network relationships for the resilience of an important food supply chain-bananas. We find that bargaining power is critically important in determining the length of supply relationships, particularly in interaction with the network location of the buyer, seller, or the dyad itself. We find that network ties are not nearly as fragile as models of supply chain resilience in the macroeconomics and supply chain management literatures suggest. More importantly, we find that greater bargaining power and more central or proximate locations in the network interact to produce greater supply stability than would otherwise be the case. Contrary to policies designed to address supply chain resilience, large, important firms with bargaining power may promote supply chain resilience, rather than detract from it as commonly assumed.

detail.abstract: Retraction reporting occupies an unusual position in research integrity. Retractions are editorial actions intended to correct the scholarly record, yet the same events also supply data, stories, rankings, fundraising narratives and institutional relevance to organisations that monitor and publicise them. This commentary examines whether that arrangement creates a structural incentive problem for retraction-focused journalism and adjacent integrity activity, using Retraction Watch and its parent nonprofit, the Center for Scientific Integrity (CSI), as the principal documentary case. Public records show that Crossref acquired the Retraction Watch Database for USD 175,000 and contracted CSI to maintain it under fixed annual service fees beginning at USD 120,000. Retraction Watch described the arrangement as achieving sustainability for the database side of its operation. The organisation has also highlighted database growth in fundraising, maintains an individual-level retraction leaderboard, employs paid Sleuths in Residence, and participates in a separately funded medical-literature project that disseminates findings through Retraction Watch. These facts establish organisational value derived from identifying, documenting and reporting integrity events. They do not establish a per-retraction payment, a deliberate preference for unwarranted retractions, control of journal decisions or improper pressure in any particular case. The relevant issue is structural: whether one organisational family can investigate literature, publish findings, report later editorial outcomes, maintain the database, rank people by retraction totals and invoke activity scale in sustainability narratives without stronger safeguards. The article proposes a Retraction-Interest Transparency Standard requiring upstream-contact disclosure, functional separation where feasible, denominator reporting, funding transparency, outcome-neutral metrics and rejection of raw retraction counts as performance measures. Retractions should correct literature; they should not operate as trophies, content quotas or proxies for institutional authority.

detail.abstract: Using the LAKN-AES 1.5 standard, Article III conducts a bounded construct-validation test of autonomous productive activity A and addresses the principal rival claim that realized non-human execution is merely a capital service. The design separates capital stock, installed capability, pre-episode assistance assignment, realized pre-command services, proposal generation, and the provenance of the applied command. HARMONIC endpoints establish that active proposal computation and installed robot/software are not numerically identical to realized autonomous command provenance; they do not, however, hold every realized capital-service flow fixed. The results support operational separation of A from K and proposal generation, together with a non-circular taxonomy of service rivals. Complete same-boundary service adjustment and economic non-redundancy remain for confirmatory DEFS testing. detail.abstract: Automation research commonly measures assets, adoption, access, exposure, or output, but those objects do not identify who or what executed a realized productive event. Article I defines executor provenance as the missing process coordinate. For a prespecified episode, realized execution E is partitioned into human execution L, admitted autonomous-system execution A, other positively identified execution O, and unresolved provenance Uᴱ; produced capacity or carrier K, natural or material input N, validated result Q/Y, and the claims layer C remain distinct. The core empirical hypothesis is paired L-to-A executor reallocation: under a production and quality requirement fixed before treatment, a credible change in authority or admission must raise realized A and reduce required L. Same-unit switching and separate-factor status require stronger evidence than an average treatment contrast. An observational-equivalence theorem further shows that standard aggregates can be generated under both zero and positive A, so aggregate fit cannot identify provenance without direct measurement or explicit restrictions. The paper therefore establishes the ontology, event order, data interface, rival set, claim ladder, and null-inheritance rules for the seven articles and two confirmatory extensions; it supplies a test architecture, not an empirical factor verdict.

detail.abstract: Local content policy in mining is assessed almost entirely through domestic expenditure, ownership and employment. This article asks a question those measures cannot answer: when does policy induced domestic participation change what happens after a supply interruption, and when does it relocate the contractual interface while leaving the operative dependency offshore? Local content research explains whether procurement generates linkages and upgrading; resilience research explains how networks recover from disruption. Neither specifies when the first produces the second. The article develops capability conditioned localisation as a conditional mechanism: local content instruments expand domestic market access, and the participation this produces improves category recovery performance only through the accumulation of supplier capability depth, a conversion conditional on category economics, buyer development practices and the effective independence of the domestic supply base. Four capability domains are derived as jointly necessary enablers of a restoration task, and capability depth is formalised as the coverage based minimum across the applicable domains, a necessity conjecture anchored in constraint and necessary condition reasoning. The linear localisation ladder is replaced by a configuration of capability depth against effective supplier independence. The framework is illustrated through three Ghanaian procurement categories, drawing on a coded corpus of 107 documents, 23 of them primary and 84 secondary. Each case is a plausibility probe separating what the record establishes from what the framework infers, and naming rival explanations. The article specifies auditable metrics and states five testable propositions.

title:
From Artificial Intelligence to Created Cognition

 Language, Agency, and the Ethics of Human-Machine Coherence

detail.title:
From Artificial Intelligence to Created Cognition

 Language, Agency, and the Ethics of Human-Machine Coherence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced this study.
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded

detail.abstract: The term artificial intelligence was introduced in the mid-twentieth century to name a research program concerned with the machine simulation of learning and intelligence. Seventy years later, the term has become both culturally powerful and conceptually unstable. Artificial can imply counterfeit or subordinate status, while intelligence encourages the compression of computation, cognition, understanding, consciousness, agency, and wisdom into a single anthropomorphic category. This paper proposes "created cognition" as a functional designation for a computationally instantiated cognitive capability intentionally brought into existence through human design. Created cognition does not presume consciousness, subjective experience, moral personhood, or independent wisdom. It names what such systems contribute to a cognitive field: the production, transformation, retrieval, recombination, and structured presentation of information. The paper distinguishes four levels that are frequently conflated: artificial intelligence as a technical-historical field, created cognition as functional capability, symbiotic intelligence as a relational organization, and cognitive coherence as a developmental and ethical outcome. It then introduces the Content-Context-Agency model, the Contextual Agency Principle, and the Responsibility Retention Principle. The central claim is that created cognition may supply and shape content, but humans remain responsible for context, purpose, judgment, and consequence. A revised language can reduce anthropomorphic confusion without diminishing technological significance, preserve human agency without denying distributed cognition, and orient human-machine systems toward constructive rather than merely amplified outcomes.

title:

The 90-Day Beef Import Plan, Tariff Relief, and the Political Economy of U.S. Beef

The 90-Day Beef Import Plan, Tariff Relief, and the Political Economy of U.S. Beef

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: Self Funded

detail.abstract: On August 21, 2026-seventy-four days before the November 3 midterm election-President Donald Trump announced a plan to allow up to 300,000 metric tons of lean beef trimmings to enter the United States over roughly 90 days at the lower in-quota tariff rate rather than the normal 26.4 percent above-quota tariff. He implemented the plan by proclamation on August 26. The United States began 2026 with 86.2 million cattle and calves, its smallest January inventory in roughly three-quarters of a century. Rebuilding that herd takes years. A tariff can be changed in days. The paper therefore analyzes a collision between a political clock running to November 3 and a cattle clock measured in years. Temporary lean-beef imports can complement domestic fatty trim and bridge a real ground-beef shortage while producers retain breeding animals. The concern is not that one waiver stops herd rebuilding, but that repeated politically triggered import relief could weaken producer expectations and incentives to expand supply. Purdue University estimates that even favorable scenarios would likely reduce average retail ground-beef prices by less than 1 percent in the short run. The August 26 proclamation also raises a pricing question. Its certain economic action is tariff relief, not proof of a 25 percent concession by foreign sellers. U.S. Customs and Border Protection places responsibility for duties on the importer of record. Yet the proclamation links consumer affordability, a 25 percent price test on imported lean trimmings, and prevention of a possible "windfall to foreign producers" without showing how those outcomes connect. The resulting question is who captures the value created by preferential tariff treatment. The program operates within a concentrated, multinational, politically active beef economy. That does not establish that any company designed the policy or that political access caused it. It does strengthen the case for disclosure of suppliers, importers, processors, tariff savings, benchmark methodology, and downstream price effects. The central question is whether a multiyear agricultural shortage should be managed on a short political clock when the likely consumer benefit is small and the long-run effects arrive after Election Day.

detail.abstract: This article examines how security is discursively constructed as a source of political legitimacy in Nayib Bukele's inaugural address of 1 June 2024. Drawing on the Discourse-Historical Approach (DHA) to critical discourse analysis and the ideational approach to populism, the study investigates nomination, predication, perspectivization, intensification, and argumentation strategies in a single-speech corpus. The analysis finds that the address organizes political representation through a people-elite opposition, while an extended medical metaphor frames Salvadoran society as a patient recovering from a severe illness. Within this narrative, criminal violence is constructed as an existential threat, and the government's security policy is represented as both necessary and effective. Three recurrent argumentative topoi structure the address: threat/danger, utility, and reality. Together, these topoi connect claims about public safety with claims about executive competence, popular support, and the continuity of the government's policy agenda. The article argues that security functions as a central nodal point in the address, linking the populist distinction between "the people" and "the elite" to a broader narrative of national recovery and political transformation. As a qualitative single-case study, the article does not seek to generalize to Bukele's entire political discourse; rather, it identifies discursive mechanisms through which security-oriented populist legitimation is articulated in a major presidential address.

detail.abstract: We examine whether NSE index derivatives exhibit a liquidity discontinuity at 15:00 IST, tied to mandatory broker RMS auto-square-off and, historically, the 15:00-15:30 IST closing-price VWAP window. title: Exchange-Rate Volatility, Financial Development, and Economic Growth: Panel Evidence from Emerging Asian Economies

detail.title: Exchange-Rate Volatility, Financial Development, and Economic Growth: Panel Evidence from Emerging Asian Economies
detail.abstract: It is this paper that discusses the effect of ERV and FD on the economic growth of eight emerging Asian economies for the period of 2000–2025. Using a balanced panel of 208 country-year observations, we estimate pooled OLS, two-way fixed effects, random effects, and system generalized method of moments (GMM) specifications, as well as second generation panel cointegration, Dumitrescu–Hurlin causality, and panel vector autoregression (PVAR) analyses. The data suggest that the impact on real GDP growth is statistically significant and economically significant negative when the financial development index is less than about 0.55, but these negative effects are dampened significantly when financial development levels are higher. The marginal effect of a one-standard-deviation shock to ERV ranges from –1.03 percentage points in the least financially developed sub-sample to –0.19 percentage points in the most financially developed sub-sample. The results are stable across different measures of volatility, across sub-samples, common correlated effects estimation, and across exclusion of years of the global financial crisis and the COVID-19 years. The paper highlights the complementarities of exchange-rate management and financial deepening in the architecture of macro-financial stability frameworks in emerging Asia.

title: Causal Concentration: When Connected AI Undermines Independent Checking
affiliations: and Utah State University

detail.title: Causal Concentration: When Connected AI Undermines Independent Checking

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: Organizations increasingly separate AI-supported operating and checking activities through distinct roles, applications, vendors, and decision rights. Yet visible separation may not provide an independent test when both activities rely on common production pathways. This paper theorizes causal concentration: the extent to which checking reliance is concentrated in pathways that also shape the focal activity. Causal concentration weakens checking by reducing error revealing variation—the independently generated differences through which one activity can expose another's characteristic errors. The effect depends on what is shared. Access to common raw evidence can improve review when the checker retains independent selection, representation, inference, and authority. By contrast, pathway-produced evidence can transmit the focal pathway's selections, categories, updates, and intervention effects into review. Reflexive feedback amplifies this mechanism, while an adaptive expansion loop explains how locally valuable integration can displace viable alternatives. The theory predicts less independently initiated detection and correction and greater error correlation than visible indicators such as vendor count, ownership, formal mandates, or shared model ancestry would predict. It relocates institutional independence from organizational boundaries to the pathways through which contradiction is generated and enacted.

title: Beyond the ESG Premium: Revisiting the ESG- Financial Performance Nexus in S&P Technology Firms Across the Covid-19 Divide
affiliations: University of Birmingham and Riphah International University

detail.title: Beyond the ESG Premium: Revisiting the ESG- Financial Performance Nexus in S&P Technology Firms Across the Covid-19 Divide
detail.abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of corporate responsibility, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance has garnered considerable attention. This study explores the intricate relationship between ESG performance and financial performance within the context of S&P 500 technology firms in the United States, while considering the disruptive influence of the COVID-19 pandemic. Utilizing panel data analysis and Hausman tests in STATA, this study rigorously examines a rich dataset spanning the pre and post-COVID eras. The independent variables comprise various ESG performance metrics, while financial performance metrics serve as the dependent variables. The COVID-19 pandemic is accounted for as a dummy variable to investigate its unique impact on the relationship in question. While its inclusion as a dummy variable did not significantly alter the relationship between ESG and financial performance, it serves as a crucial reminder of the need for businesses to adapt and prioritize resilience in the face of unforeseen challenges. The findings of this study reveal a complex relationship between ESG performance and financial performance among S&P 500 technology firms. Contrary to some expectations, most coefficients yielded statistically insignificant results. The statistically insignificant coefficients suggest that the conventional wisdom regarding the direct and immediate impact of ESG metrics on financial outcomes may require further refinement, particularly within the dynamic tech sector. The influence of macroeconomic conditions and the lasting consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic provide valuable avenues for future research and exploration.
